rods.name: Bamboo Rod
rods.description: A simple bamboo pole. Gets the job done.

rods.name: Driftwood Staff
rods.description: Heavy and slow, but the wide tip gives you a more forgiving catch window.

rods.name: Fiberglass Rod
rods.description: Lighter than bamboo with a wider tip. Gives you a more forgiving catch window.

rods.name: Reef Guard
rods.description: Responsive and fast. Bites come a little quicker than the baseline.

rods.name: Telescoping Rod
rods.description: Extends deep. Something about the length draws rarer fish to the surface.

rods.name: Moonwood Staff
rods.description: Carved from driftwood blessed by a full moon. Quicker bites and a wider catch window.

rods.name: Graphite Rod
rods.description: Lightweight and stiff. Noticeably quicker bites.

rods.name: Navigator's Rod
rods.description: A well-balanced deep-sea rod. Good speed and a wider catch zone.

rods.name: Carbon Rod
rods.description: Precision-engineered for quick, snappy bites.

rods.name: Deep Diver
rods.description: Built for the abyss. Fast bites and a wide catch window.

rods.name: Legendary Rod
rods.description: Forged from the mast of a sunken galleon. Faster bites, and the rarest fish cannot resist.

rods.name: Twin-Strike
rods.description: Two hooks on one line. When luck strikes, they both bite.

rods.name: Second Wind
rods.description: Stubborn rod. When you miss, sometimes it refuses to let go.

rods.name: Millionaire's Rod
rods.description: Hand-rolled in gold leaf. Every catch brings two.

rods.name: YOLO Rod
rods.description: Roll the dice every cast for a 100-fish haul — and the odds climb the shallower you fish. The rest of the time? Just a regular catch.

rods.name: Completionist Rod
rods.description: Forged from the soul of every species in the sea. A master's tool on its own, and a vessel besides: fit up to three rods you own into it to carry their gifts, and re-forge whenever you like.

rods.name: Treasure Rod
rods.description: Lures the deep’s lost hoards — doubles your chance of hooking a crate.

rods.name: Perfect Rod
rods.description: Rewards flawless form — perfect catches grant double XP, and it scales with your streak.

rods.name: Galaxy Rod
rods.description: Spun from cosmic thread. After any catch, open a wormhole and reroll it into a different fish from the same waters — fortune or folly, you take what surfaces.

rods.name: Lightsaber Rod
rods.description: A blade of pure energy. Fish are drawn to the light — most casts bite almost the instant your line touches the water.

rods.name: Yoon's Locked-In Rod
rods.description: Rewards a hot hand. Chain perfect catches to LOCK IN: 3 in a row quickens your bites, 5 lands a triple haul on every catch, and 10 quickens them further into a rare-fish frenzy. Hold the streak to keep it all — one miss and you start over.

baits.name: Worms
baits.description: Reliable all-purpose bait. Claim 20 free from your Daily Bonus.

baits.name: Night Crawler
baits.description: Fish bite 15% faster. Widens your catch zone by 4° — a bigger catch zone means more room to land the needle.

baits.name: Angler's Formula
baits.description: Fish bite 35% faster. Widens your catch zone by 8° — a bigger catch zone means more room to land the needle.

baits.name: Luminous Lure
baits.description: Fish bite 40% faster and the catch zone widens by 10°. Earned from expeditions and bounties, or bought with Fathoms in the Locker. Something ancient stirs when it glows.
baits.hint: Something ancient stirs when it glows.

baits.name: Golden Lure
baits.description: Fish bite 45% faster. Widens your catch zone by 10°. The finest lure in existence — a rare drop, or bought with Fathoms in the Locker. The oldest things in the deep rise for its shine.
baits.hint: The oldest things in the deep rise for its shine.

lines.name: Copolymer
lines.description: Blended nylon. More give, less break.

lines.name: Titanium Wire
lines.description: Near-zero stretch. Cuts through current like nothing.

lines.name: Deep Sea Line
lines.description: Built for the abyss. Almost nothing breaks it.

reels.name: Basic Reel
reels.description: Gets the job done. The needle moves fast though.

reels.name: Spinning Reel
reels.description: Smoother drag. A little more time to react.

reels.name: Baitcasting Reel
reels.description: Precision drag control. The needle slows noticeably.

reels.name: Saltwater Reel
reels.description: Built for the open sea. Solid drag, steady needle.

reels.name: Precision Reel
reels.description: Tournament-grade. You feel every twitch of the line.

reels.name: Tournament Reel
reels.description: Competition-spec drag. The needle moves like it has something to prove.

reels.name: Deep Sea Reel
reels.description: Engineered for the deep. The needle barely hurries.

reels.name: Kraken's Grip
reels.description: Forged to hold something ancient. The needle drifts, almost lazy.

reels.name: Tidecaller's Reel
reels.description: Time itself seems to slow when you reel. Almost unfair.

hooks.name: Copper Hook
hooks.description: A simple copper hook. Reliable enough to land your first catch.

hooks.name: Bronze Hook
hooks.description: Forged bronze. A touch sturdier than copper.

hooks.name: Iron Hook
hooks.description: Solid iron. A noticeably wider catch window.

hooks.name: Steel Hook
hooks.description: Tempered steel. Reliable in any depth.

hooks.name: Silver Hook
hooks.description: Polished silver. Catches the light — and the fish.

hooks.name: Gold Hook
hooks.description: Polished gold. Fish can't resist the shine.

hooks.name: Enchanted Hook
hooks.description: Glows faintly. Something stirs in the deep.

hooks.name: Abyssal Hook
hooks.description: Drawn from the dark. The catch window is remarkably wide.

hooks.name: Legendary Hook
hooks.description: Said to have been lost at sea — and returned.

sharpshot.name: Sharpshot
sharpshot.blurb: Widens the gold crit zone on your next shots. By the top tiers, any clean hit crits.

milestones.desc: Next shot crit zone 60% wider.
Next shot crit zone doubled.
Next shot crit zone nearly tripled.
Next 2 shots crit zone 3.5× wider.
Next 2 shots crit zone 4× wider.
Next 3 shots crit zone 4.5× wider. A clean hit almost always crits.

snare.name: Snare
snare.blurb: Disables the enemy's dodge for several turns. Always lands.

milestones.desc: 20% chance to jam enemy dodge for 2 turns.
30% chance to jam enemy dodge for 2 turns.
40% chance to jam enemy dodge for 2 turns.
48% chance to jam enemy dodge for 3 turns.
54% chance to jam enemy dodge for 4 turns.
60% chance to jam enemy dodge for 5 turns.

anchor.name: Anchor
anchor.blurb: Absorbs a portion of the next incoming hit. Dependable wall, not a coin flip.

milestones.desc: Reduce next incoming hit by 20%.
Reduce next incoming hit by 30%.
Reduce next incoming hit by 45%.
Reduce next incoming hit by 60%.
Reduce next incoming hit by 80%.
Reduce next incoming hit by 95% (even crits).

navigator.name: Navigator
navigator.blurb: Chance to grant the player a charge instantly. Better odds at higher levels.

milestones.desc: 30% chance to gain +1 charge.
40% chance to gain +1 charge.
60% chance to gain +1 charge.
80% chance to gain +1 charge.
Always gain +1 charge. 20% chance for +2.
Always gain +1 charge. 50% chance for +2.

abyssal_tide.name: Tidecaller
abyssal_tide.blurb: Heals the ship and grants a temporary damage shield. Heal now, brace for what's coming.

milestones.desc: Heal 14% max HP and grant a 5% max HP shield.
Heal 20% max HP and grant an 8% max HP shield.
Heal 30% max HP and grant an 11% max HP shield.
Heal 40% max HP and grant a 14% max HP shield.
Heal 50% max HP and grant a 17% max HP shield.
Heal 60% max HP, grant a 20% max HP shield, and cleanse one enemy debuff.

leviathan.name: Leviathan
leviathan.blurb: Fires one massive extra cannon shot. A single, ship-shaking crit that ALWAYS lands the full crit amount. Made for big prey: the heavy shell is largely wasted on regular hulls, but it hits far harder against bosses and elites.

milestones.desc: Fire 1 heavy crit shot. −45% vs regular hulls, +20% vs bosses and elites.
Fire 1 heavy crit shot. −45% vs regular hulls, +25% vs bosses and elites.
Fire 1 heavy crit shot. −45% vs regular hulls, +35% vs bosses and elites.
Fire 1 heavy crit shot. −45% vs regular hulls, +45% vs bosses and elites.
Fire 1 bigger heavy crit shot. −45% vs regular hulls, +55% vs bosses and elites.
Fire 1 massive heavy crit shot. −45% vs regular hulls, +65% vs bosses and elites.

blitz.name: Apex
blitz.blurb: A feeding frenzy of light shots. A fixed barrage that never whiffs and BITES HARDER the more wounded the target is. Middling on a fresh hull, devastating as a finisher.

milestones.desc: Fire a 2-shot barrage at 28% damage each. Up to +15% per shot as the target weakens.
Fire a 3-shot barrage at 28% damage each. Up to +20% per shot as the target weakens.
Fire a 4-shot barrage at 28% each. Up to +25% as the target weakens.
Fire a 5-shot barrage at 28% each. Up to +35% as the target weakens.
Fire a 6-shot barrage at 30% each. Up to +45% as the target weakens.
Fire an 8-shot barrage at 30% each. Up to +60% per shot as the target weakens.

foresight.name: Oracle
foresight.blurb: Reveals the enemy's next moves. At higher ranks, refreshes your dodge so you can slip a shot you already spent your dodge on.

milestones.desc: See the enemy's next move.
See the enemy's next move.
See the enemy's next 2 moves.
See the next 2 moves; 30% chance to refresh your dodge.
See the next 3 moves; 50% chance to refresh your dodge.
See the next 3 moves and always refresh your dodge.

vengeance.name: Vengeance
vengeance.blurb: Arm a vengeance ward for 3 turns. Take a killing blow while it burns and you cheat death: heal part of your hull and surge with bonus damage for the rest of the fight. Let it run out and it is wasted.

milestones.desc: Arm the ward for 3 turns. Cheat a killing blow while it burns: heal 18% max HP, gain +10% damage for the rest of the fight.
Arm the ward for 3 turns. Cheat a killing blow while it burns: heal 25% max HP, gain +15% damage for the rest of the fight.
Arm the ward for 3 turns. Cheat a killing blow while it burns: heal 25% max HP, gain +20% damage for the rest of the fight.
Arm the ward for 3 turns. Cheat a killing blow while it burns: heal 35% max HP, gain +25% damage for the rest of the fight.
Arm the ward for 3 turns. Cheat a killing blow while it burns: heal 35% max HP, gain +30% damage for the rest of the fight.
Arm the ward for 3 turns. Cheat a killing blow while it burns: heal 50% max HP, gain +35% damage for the rest of the fight, and cleanse every debuff.

requiem.name: Requiem
requiem.blurb: Marks the enemy for death. While the mark burns, that target takes bonus damage from everything. Your shots and every crew ability. She deals no damage herself; the whole crew collects. At the cap, a marked enemy's shield is ignored.

milestones.desc: Mark the enemy for 2 turns. It takes +10% damage from all sources.
Mark the enemy for 2 turns. It takes +15% damage from all sources.
Mark the enemy for 2 turns. It takes +18% damage from all sources.
Mark the enemy for 3 turns. It takes +22% damage from all sources.
Mark the enemy for 3 turns. It takes +25% damage from all sources.
Mark the enemy for 3 turns. It takes +25% damage from all sources, and its shield is ignored while marked.

hallTiers.name: Driftwood Hall
hallTiers.flavor: Salvaged planks, a leaky roof, and one bunk in the corner.

hallTiers.name: Oakhewn Hall
hallTiers.flavor: Solid oak beams and room to drill. Word spreads.

hallTiers.name: Brassbound Hall
hallTiers.flavor: Brass fittings, a proper bar, and bunks that see real use.

hallTiers.name: Gilded Hall
hallTiers.flavor: Gold leaf on the rafters, and drillmasters who know their trade.

hallTiers.name: Hall of Legends
hallTiers.flavor: Names sung in every port. Every hand who bunks here leaves it sharper.

hallTiers.name: Leviathan Hall
hallTiers.flavor: Rafters cut from something that used to swim. The deepest bunk still remembers it.

shinyMessages: A golden {fish}. The kind of catch sailors carve into the hull.
{fish} of gold under your hand. Captain, this is one in a thousand.
Sailors tell tales of gold-scaled ones. Tonight you've held one.
A gilded {fish} — the sea's own coin. Mount it, or part with it for a king's haul.
Gold-scaled and impossible. Even the old captains only saw one of these.
A {fish} drawn up in solid gold. The dockside won't believe you without proof.
Worth more than a hold of common haul, and rarer than the stories about it.
The crew has gone quiet. None of them have ever seen a golden one before.
A golden {fish}. Every captain hopes for this once in a career.
The deep turned a {fish} to gold tonight, and gave it to you.

lines.text: ...*Megalodon.*
The last one. The one all the others were only ever leading up to.
All six. In a single pair of hands.
Do you have any notion what you have just finished building?
Years I stood at that black water, and it would not open for me. Not one inch. And you...
You were exactly what it was waiting for. Exactly what *I* was waiting for.
Never mind. Old rivals get sentimental.
Go on. Enjoy your wall of monsters.
The long-neck. *Plesiosaurus.* I have watched that thing take a rig and swim off like it felt nothing.
It let you land it. Sat in your hands like it decided to.
The deep does not just decide. Not for most of us.
Hm. Go on, then.
*Dunkleosteus.* A jaw like a ship's prow, older than the first keel that ever cut this water.
I hooked it once. It took my line and left me the story. That is all it has ever left anyone.
It handed you the whole fish. I would sit a while with why.
...or do not. Just keep pulling them up.
*Mosasaurus.* The sea-dragon every old chart drew a hard border around.
Turns out that border was the only honest ink on the page.
Every soul who chased these is a name cut in stone now. Every one but you.
That was never luck. Luck drowned a long way back. You are something the water wants.
The *Basilosaurus.* It swam this water before there was a single soul alive to fear it.
I have wanted to look one of these in the eye my whole life. Never once got the chance.
And here it lies on your deck, dripping like a market cod.
Sits wrong, does it not. ...Good. It ought to.
*Shastasaurus.* The largest thing that ever drew breath in salt water, and it is on your hook.
The others all swore these were stories. Easier than admitting they were out of reach.
They were never out of yours. The deep keeps handing you what it kept from me.
...from everyone. So keep pulling, captain. I mean to see just how far those hands of yours can reach.

nodes.label: A Loose Thread
nodes.flavor: Barnacle Pete... the famed pirate captain who's been robbing these shores for years. No one's ever stopped him because he only pounces on the weak.
nodes.bridge: Every thread runs back to the same reef. Pete doesn't do his own collecting, so his crew are the ones you meet first.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Now that you've got your ship and a crew, let's take care of some business. It's been far too long since someone put a stop on Barnacle Pete.
He's robbed the weak and poor for years. All up and down this coast.
Little crew. Fishing folk. The odd unlucky angler. Anyone too small to swing back.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: And here's the part that doesn't make sense. Pete steals so much but never has anything to show for it.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: I think it's time we do something about it. We've scouted him out just further down the waters.

scene.speaker: Barnacle Pete
scene.text: Heard there's some new folk in town to plunder.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Charming, isn't he? Let's go shake him up and see what he's up to.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Remember, if you don't feel like you're ready, go back and make sure you get some stronger crew aboard!

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Can always learn the hard way. Onward!

detail.description:
Barnacle Pete is famous, and nobody has ever stopped him. That isn't because he's hard to find. It's because he only ever picks the fights he knows he wins. Little crew, fishing folk, the odd unlucky angler. Anyone too small to swing back.

What doesn't make sense is the money. Pete has robbed this coast for years and has nothing to show for it. He never gets to spend any of it. He just delivers it, and no one will say who to. You've got a ship and a crew now, so go and find out.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment I
drops.sublabel: "They say Pete never gets to spend anything. He just delivers it." Said once, by a sailor who never said it again.

detail.dropsNote: Pages like this pile up the more you go poking around. Sooner or later they spell out a name.
detail.summary: Pete has robbed this coast for years and kept none of it. Every haul goes somewhere else, and you mean to find out where.

nodes.label: Reef Skirmish
nodes.flavor: Pete keeps his own hands clean and his Reef Raiders busy. Time to start putting them on the seabed.
nodes.bridge: Thin out his Raiders and you thin out his nerve. Sink enough and the old corsair rows out himself to see who's been counting.

detail.description:
Pete's not the type to do his own swinging. That's what the Reef Raiders are for, and the reef's crawling with them. Sink one and another bobs up grinning to take the empty seat.

No grand plan out here. Pick them off, one soggy thug at a time, and wait to see who comes asking once too many of them stop rowing home.
detail.dropsNote: Pete never runs short of Raiders. Swing by and trim the numbers whenever the mood takes you.

nodes.label: The Corsair's Reckoning
nodes.flavor: Barnacle Pete and his fleet are out in the open at last. He has never had a real fight in his life. Give him one.
nodes.bridge: Pete goes down, and his strongbox spills more than coin. Ledgers. A sealed letter. The famous Barnacle Pete has been running someone else's errands this whole time.

detail.description:
Four ship battles back to back, each one harder than the last, with no time to patch up between them. Pete waits at the end of it.

He has never been pushed by anyone who could swing back, and he fights like it. Win the run and his crate finally opens. It's the only place his contraband ever turns up.

drops.label: Finndicate Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Corsair Cannon
drops.sublabel: Raid item. +10% damage to raid bosses.

drops.label: Corsair's Prime Cannon
drops.sublabel: Raid item. +20% damage to raid bosses. The captain-grade version of the Corsair Cannon.

detail.dropsNote: One crate per Pete clear, rolled once and scaled by your Fortune. Every kill along the way also pays gold + Nav XP.

nodes.label: Challenge: The Corsair's Reckoning
nodes.flavor: Pete sails out again, meaner this time, with the kind of crew that doesn't lose twice.

detail.description: Same six ship battles, same old corsair at the end, but every hull he's put back on the water is a step harder than the last. The Raiders hit cleaner, the Marksman aims truer, and Pete fights like a captain who's finally noticed you're still here. Crack his crate this time and the contraband runs richer for it.

drops.label: Finndicate Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Corsair Cannon
drops.sublabel: Raid item. +10% damage to raid bosses.

detail.dropsNote: Every kill pays more, the clear bonus is steeper, and his unique contraband rolls at double the normal rate.

nodes.label: Up the Line
nodes.flavor: Pete's books all name the same outfit: the Finndicate. One sealed letter points past them, at somebody called C.K.
nodes.bridge: The letter's heading runs straight through the Bilge Strait. To follow C.K.'s cargo you have to get past the thugs who own that water first.

scene.text: You find Pete's strongbox. But there's no treasure inside. Just... paperwork?
Cut sheets. Courier routes. Years of accounting.
One word is stamped on every page: *the Finndicate*.

scene.speaker: Barnacle Pete
scene.text: You think I keep the coin? Not a doubloon stays with me.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Hmm... Pete was nothing but a pawn. He works for someone else. No wonder he plundered so much and had so little to show for it.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: The Finndicate. I've heard the name. They control the outer seas... but they're mostly involved in commercial business. Why would Pete involve himself...
The pages say the same thing over and over again. Funds needed for purchases, but no reason behind them.
Under the ledgers there is a sealed letter. No name, but two initials: *C.K.*
The route is mostly burned away, but you make out a path out past the Bilge Strait.
Whoever C.K. is, the Finndicate trusts them with the cargo. Seems like many small captains like Barnacle Pete are shipping their plunder to him.
You notice that someone's been trailing you for a while now... you've felt their presence ever since you came into Pete's quarters.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Hmm... the Bilge Strait huh? Most captains wouldn't sail through there just based on a hunch. Good thing neither of us is the average captain.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Name's Mako. Common enemy means we're partners. I've been trying to lock down Pete for a while now. Seems like we had a common goal. Muster a crew and my name's on the table.
Mako joins the campaign. He is now also recruitable as a crew for your ship.

detail.description:
The strongbox held no treasure, just paperwork. Cut sheets, courier routes, years of accounting, and one word stamped on every page: the Finndicate. Pete was never the kingpin. He was a pawn working for someone else, which explains how he plundered so much and had so little to show for it.

The Finndicate control the outer seas, and they are mostly a commercial outfit, which is the part that doesn't fit. The pages ask for funds over and over and never once say what the purchases are for. Under the ledgers there is a sealed letter, no name, two initials pressed into the wax: C.K. The route is mostly burned away, but it runs out past the Bilge Strait. Whoever C.K. is, small captains like Pete have been shipping their plunder to him.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment II
drops.sublabel: "The Finndicate doesn't lose captains. It loses ledgers." Scratched into the underside of the strongbox lid.

drops.label: Sealed Shipment Letter
drops.sublabel: Addressed to "C.K." and nobody else. A heavy manifest, bound past the Bilge Strait.

detail.dropsNote: A name to chase (the Finndicate) and a lead to follow (C.K., and the way the cargo runs). Both run straight through the Bilge Strait.
detail.summary: Pete's strongbox held no treasure, just ledgers naming the Finndicate and a sealed letter marked C.K., with a route running out past the Bilge Strait.

nodes.label: The Bilge Eels
nodes.flavor: The Bilge Eels report to nobody and serve only doubloons. Every hull that crosses their strait pays, and C.K.'s freight crossed it too.
nodes.bridge: Past the strait the water turns Finndicate. C.K.'s cargo is moving somewhere ahead, and there's a keeper up there with a counter and no name to give.

scene.text: You've made it to the Bilge Strait. Lucky you.
You're not alone though. The strait belongs to the Bilge Eels... now that name makes sense.

scene.speaker: A Bilge Eel
scene.text: Far enough, captain. You're crossing into our waters now.

scene.speaker: A Bilge Eel
scene.text: We don't report to anyone but ourselves. And the only master we serve is doubloons.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: These greedy rats... I mean eels.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: They've only ever cared about coin.
It's hard to stay neutral in this territory, but looks like the Bilge Eels control a water that has made them richer. And they're ones to take advantage of that situation.

scene.speaker: A Bilge Eel
scene.text: We see a lot of freight sailing these waters. And they all gotta pay us.

scene.speaker: A Bilge Eel
scene.text: 1,000 doubloons gets you a smooth crossing. And we'll forget we ever saw ya.
Doesn't seem like there's another way around.
Looks like you gotta pay up or earn enough to get through.

detail.description:
The letter's heading runs out past the Bilge Strait, and the strait belongs to the Bilge Eels. Two banks and a gap barely wide enough for a couple of hulls, which is the whole reason they can charge for it.

They report to nobody and serve only doubloons. Not the Finndicate, not you. They sit on the one crossing that points where C.K.'s cargo went and they take a cut of everything that passes, because there is no way around. Pay them 1,000 ⟡ and the way opens onto C.K.'s trail. Keep your purse shut and you go no further.

drops.label: The trail toward C.K.
drops.sublabel: Passage through the strait, hard on C.K.'s heading.

detail.dropsNote: A one-time bribe. The 1,000 ⟡ is spent for good, not held or refunded.
detail.summary: The Bilge Eels own the only crossing on C.K.'s heading and serve nothing but doubloons. A thousand of them bought the passage, and C.K.'s trail runs on past the strait.

nodes.label: Quartermaster's Cache
nodes.flavor: Past the strait, a keeper called the Quartermaster lays out two bits of contraband and lets you walk off with exactly one.
nodes.bridge: The Quartermaster sells a lot less than he lets on. The cold water ahead answers to one captain, and the wax on Pete's letter finally has a name behind it.

scene.text: Past the strait, someone has made a counter out of a wrecked hull and a barrel, and is waiting behind it.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Two things on the barrel, captain. You take one.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: I don't haggle and I don't repeat myself.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Everyone who crosses that strait ends up at my counter sooner or later. You'll be back.

detail.description:
The keeper on the far shore of the Bilge Strait calls himself the Quartermaster and doesn't offer a name past it. He sets two bits of contraband on the barrel between you, the sort that doesn't wash up twice, and tells you to pick. One. The other slides back into the cache and out of your life for good.

Whatever you take is yours to keep, ready to equip in your raid loadout with the rest of your kit.
detail.dropsNote: Pick one. Permanent, equippable, and you can't come back for the other.

nodes.label: The Name on the Wax
nodes.flavor: Two letters in a blot of wax, and a name behind them at last. Captain Krust moves the Finndicate's freight, and lately most of it is stolen.
nodes.bridge: Captain Krust. He runs the Finndicate's freight, and every hold he fills is a hold you can empty. His consignment's out on the water right now.

scene.text: All this travel just for two letters: C.K.
Now we know.
*Captain Krust*.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Krust. He's in charge of moving the Finndicate's freight.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: The Finndicate must trust him. He must know he's taking in stolen goods.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Smarter than Pete for sure.
Krust has been moving commercial goods for ages. But these days, it looks like he's funneling more stolen cargo than actual goods.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: His activities are suspicious.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Definitely. Someone is behind all of this... but we'll have to get through Krust to see what's going on.
Krust's goals are uncertain. But it'll certainly be harder to get through to Krust than Pete.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Ready your guns, captain. His crew spotted us!

detail.description:
All that travel for two letters, and now there is a name behind them: Captain Krust.

Krust runs the Finndicate's freight. He has moved commercial goods for ages, long enough that nobody looks twice at his manifests, and these days he is funneling more stolen cargo than actual goods. The Finndicate trust him with it, which means he knows exactly what he is taking in. He is nothing like Pete, and he will be a great deal harder to get through. Someone is behind all of this, and Krust is the way to them.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment III
drops.sublabel: "More stolen cargo than honest goods, and the manifests say neither." What Pete's courier routes add up to once you have the name.

detail.dropsNote: A name at last. The Finndicate's freight has a face, and that face knows exactly what it is carrying.
detail.summary: The wax finally had a name behind it: Captain Krust, the hand the Finndicate trusts with all its freight. He knows exactly what he is carrying, and he is the way to whoever is above him.

nodes.label: Krust's Consignment
nodes.flavor: Captain Krust's freight runs the cold water past the Bilge Strait. Sink the consignment and the Finndicate feels every lost crate.
nodes.bridge: Krust goes down and his manifest goes over the side with him. He was no kingpin either. Whatever he was hauling, someone further up the line is already missing it.

detail.description:
Krust's full run in one go: six ship battles through his consignment crew, each heavier than the last, no breather anywhere in it, and the old captain waiting at the end on his iron-sided carrack.

Every hull in this crew is crustacean, all shell and spite, so a slice of your fire just glances off them, and Krust shrugs off more still. He has owned this cold water long enough to think nobody can take it from him. Sink the lot and his crate splits open, the only place his contraband ever drops. Nothing on Pete's reef sailed half this hard.

drops.label: Finndicate Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Krust's Carapace
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Cuts incoming enemy fire by 10%.

drops.label: Captain's Carapace
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Cuts incoming enemy fire by 15%. The plated hide Krust himself hid behind for years.

detail.dropsNote: One crate per Krust clear, rolled once and scaled by your Fortune. Every kill along the way also pays gold + Nav XP.

nodes.label: Challenge: Krust's Consignment
nodes.flavor: Krust patched the iron hull, drilled the crew, and put the consignment back on the cold water. He doesn't lose cargo twice.

detail.description: Krust's full consignment again, harder for the loss. The Carapace runs thicker, the volleys land cleaner, and every hand on his deck has had a long, cold look at the captain who already sank them once. Crack the crate this run and the contraband rolls deeper than any of his first manifests ever paid.

drops.label: Finndicate Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Krust's Carapace
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Cuts incoming enemy fire by 10%.

drops.label: Captain's Carapace
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Cuts incoming enemy fire by 15%. The plated hide Krust himself hid behind for years.

detail.dropsNote: Every kill pays more, the clear bonus is steeper, and his unique contraband rolls at double the normal rate.

nodes.label: Between Watches
nodes.flavor: Two captains under, and a rare quiet on the deck. Before the next heading, the crew takes a watch together.
nodes.bridge: The rest never lasts. Somewhere past the dark water, the Finndicate has started asking who you are.

scene.text: You watch as Krust's consignment burns to the waterline. The Finndicate will feel this soon.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: It's time to rest up, cap'n. Krust is no more.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Krust is gone, but a lot of questions remain.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: For one, we're definitely on the Finndicate's list now.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: But maybe that's what we need in order to track down what's next.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Somehow encouraging yet terrifying.
Somewhere past the dark water, something large stops what it's doing to look your way.
But that's a problem for another day. Tonight the crew is whole, and the grog is cold.

detail.description:
Pete and Krust are both on the seabed and the consignment burned to the waterline. The Finndicate will feel this one soon.

Krust is gone and the questions are not. You are on their list now, which Mako reckons is the fastest way to find out who is above them. Tomorrow that will matter. Tonight the crew is whole and the grog is cold.
detail.summary: With Pete and Krust both under, the crew took a quiet watch together before the next heading. You are on the Finndicate's list now, which may be the fastest way to whoever is above them.

nodes.label: Captain's Choice
nodes.flavor: Two captains on the seabed and the Finndicate's attention squarely on you. Time to decide what kind of captain you want to be.

detail.description: You sank Pete. You sank Krust. You are on the Finndicate's list now, and the water past here won't be kind. Stand on your deck and pick a class. Once it's chosen it stays with you for every raid from here on.

nodes.label: Crate by Crate
nodes.flavor: Krust's hold is three days of crates and not one of them worth stealing. Whatever the Finndicate has been paying for, it was never plunder.
nodes.bridge: Every crate Krust moved was survey gear, and all of it was going to one chartmaker. Dole matched the heading, and it runs out past the danger line.

scene.text: Three laborious days going through everything in Krust's hold... crate by crate by crate. Nothing of value was getting sent out. But there is a pattern.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Instruments. Sounding lines... oil, glass. What is the purpose of all of this?

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: There's something specific they're after.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Where is this all going to?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: A chartmaker.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Who are you?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Dole. I've dabbled in charting myself. This is all survey gear, friends. I've been trying to find out who's been stealing my goods and where it's all gone.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: A chartmaker? Shouldn't the Finndicate know their way around by now?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Around the known parts, yes. But those aren't the parts a chartmaker gets paid for.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: You know who they're paying then?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: I had a hunch. But I've confirmed it now that you all took down Krust. I was able to match the heading to where the shipments would go to.
Dole sets a map down facing you.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: I'd be happy to help out. The northern seas aren't for the blind.
Dole joins the party. You are now able to recruit him as well.

detail.description:
Three days in Krust's hold, crate by crate, and almost none of it is worth stealing. Instruments. Sounding line by the mile. Blank vellum, oil, glass. Survey gear, all of it.

The Finndicate has not been getting rich off what it takes. It has been buying supplies for one chartmaker and paying with everything Pete and Krust ever moved. Dole turns up while the crew are still arguing about it: a chartmaker himself, robbed by the same outfit, who has spent years trying to find out where his own goods went. Krust's fall gave him the last piece. He has the heading now, and he is willing to sail it with you.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment IV
drops.sublabel: "Instruments, sounding line, vellum, oil, glass. Not one crate of it worth stealing." The manifest of Krust's last run, in your own hand.

detail.dropsNote: Not plunder. Supplies, bought with everything they ever stole, and a heading that says who for.
detail.summary: Krust's hold held no plunder, only survey gear. The Finndicate has been funding one chartmaker with everything it steals, and Dole matched the heading to where the shipments go.

nodes.label: The Smuggler's Chart
nodes.flavor: Krust's cabin gave up the freight network map: every drop on the coast strung onto one chain of signal beacons. Light the whole chain at once and you see how much of it there is.
nodes.bridge: Every beacon on the coast burns for one chartmaker's survey. Dole had the heading right, and the size of the thing feeding it is the part nobody was meant to read.

puzzle.reveal:
The beacons hold, the whole chain steady at last, and the map gives up its secret. Every lane, every drop, every night run on this coast, all of it feeding one chartmaker past the danger line.

Dole had the heading right. What he did not have was the scale of it.

detail.description:
Krust was no kingpin, just a captain who ran cargo, and the Finndicate keeps its captains roped to each other. His cabin gave up the network map: a chain of signal beacons, each drop wired to the next, lit only on the nights the freight runs.

The chain's rigged against prying eyes. Light one beacon and the lanterns either side of it flare or gutter, so no single light ever gives the shape away. Get them all burning at once and the whole apparatus shows itself: every drop on this coast, and the one survey it has been feeding.

drops.label: 500 Nav XP
drops.sublabel: Reading the whole network sharpens your navigation. No coin in it, just the shape of the thing.

detail.dropsNote: Tap beacons to light the chain. Each tap flips the one you touch and its neighbors. Light them all at once to read the network. One-time, no cost, no fight.

nodes.label: Driftwood Cache
nodes.flavor: The Quartermaster has a driftwood shack on a rock just inside the danger line. Two bits of kit on the counter, take one, leave the other for good.

scene.text: A driftwood shack hammered to a rock, a counter already laid out, and the same keeper behind it.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Told you. Two on the barrel, captain. Same rules as the strait.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: You're wondering how I got out here first. Everybody does. Nobody asks twice.

detail.description:
Past the beacon chain the chart shows another drop point, a driftwood shack hammered to a rock just inside the danger line. The same counter, the same keeper, the same trick he pulled past the strait: two bits of kit on the barrel, take one, leave the other for good. He got here before you did, and he will be there the next time too.

Whatever you take is yours to keep, ready to equip in your raid loadout with the rest of your kit.
detail.dropsNote: Pick one. Permanent, equippable, and you can't come back for the other.

nodes.label: The Charts That Don't Exist
nodes.flavor: Two scout cutters running the water ahead of you. No flag, and neither one's anything like a freight ship. You catch them clean.
nodes.bridge: The scouts sail off, one way or another, and word of your name runs through the cold water faster than any chart of yours could chase it.

scene.text: You see two cutters sailing tight together. No flags. Neither one is built to carry freight.
They're sounding the water right ahead of you.
You catch them.

scene.speaker: A Caught Scout
scene.text: What do you want from us? You'll get nothing here.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Who do you work for?

scene.speaker: A Caught Scout
scene.text: We ain't telling you anything!

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Do you work for the Finndicate?

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: What should we do, captain?

choices.label: Sack the hold
choices.description: Take the coin in their strongbox and send the empty hulls home. Word goes round the docks that you run poor on principle and rich on plunder.

choices.label: Cut them loose
choices.description: Send them back untouched, no message. A captain who keeps to the high water looks after his own, and sometimes that earns him a sail in his lee when he needs one. The cold water has a long memory.

choices.label: Take the navigator's logs
choices.description: Leave the coin, take the charts. The marks on them sharpen every heading you sail from here on, even the ones you can't read yet.

detail.description:
Two cutters sailing tight together, no flags, and neither one built to carry freight. They were sounding the water right ahead of you, which is the water the chartmaker has been paid to map. You catch them clean.

They will not say who they work for. Asked straight out whether it's the Finndicate, they say nothing at all, and the nothing is the answer. Scouts sound water for somebody, and somebody out here wants this stretch known before you know it.

The choice is yours. Pick once, and only once.
detail.dropsNote: One-time event. Pick your option and you sail on. The water past this point has already been charted by somebody, and you have not met him yet.
detail.summary: Two Finndicate scout cutters, caught clean past the danger line. They never gave a name, but the cargo and the cut of the ships said plenty. You made your call and sailed on.

nodes.label: The Cartographer's Survey
nodes.flavor: Past the Finndicate scouts the water turns to gray wall. The galleon waiting in the fog drew every chart Krust ever followed. Sink him and the Finndicate loses its eyes.
nodes.bridge: His ship goes down with no flag and no name on the hull. The charts in his cabin were nearly finished, and whatever they were being finished for, he never said.

detail.description: The Finndicate's chartmaker rides a slow-built galleon under the fog past the danger line, and every freight lane Krust ever ran, he drew first. His crew sails the Sounding Fog for cover, so every aim through it lands a half-read short. And he counters a dodge with a brass-bound parry few captains see coming twice. Cut his hull and the chart line goes down with him.

drops.label: Chartmaker Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Cartographer's Astrolabe
drops.sublabel: Raid item. On a successful dodge, 30% chance to deflect 50% of the incoming shot back at the attacker.

drops.label: Mastercraft Astrolabe
drops.sublabel: Raid item. On a successful dodge, 50% chance to deflect 75% of the incoming shot back at the attacker. The Cartographer's own brass instrument, machined to a finer tolerance than any other in his cabin.

detail.dropsNote: One crate per Cartographer clear, rolled once and scaled by your Fortune. Every kill along the way pays gold + Nav XP, and the run carries two Tide events between fights. Read them and choose.

nodes.label: Challenge: The Cartographer's Survey
nodes.flavor: The chartmaker put a fresh hull under the fog and a tighter watch on the line. He doesn't lose seas twice.

detail.description: The same chart line again, sharper for the loss. The fog runs heavier, the Surveyor reads the water cleaner, and the Cartographer counters every dodge like a captain who's already seen this fight once. Crack his cabin this run and his own astrolabe rolls at twice the rate.

drops.label: Chartmaker Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Cartographer's Astrolabe
drops.sublabel: Raid item. On a successful dodge, 30% chance to deflect 50% of the incoming shot back at the attacker.

drops.label: Mastercraft Astrolabe
drops.sublabel: Raid item. On a successful dodge, 50% chance to deflect 75% of the incoming shot back at the attacker. The Cartographer's own brass instrument, machined to a finer tolerance than any other in his cabin.

detail.dropsNote: Every kill pays more, the clear bonus is steeper, and the legendary Captain's Astrolabe rolls at double the normal rate.

nodes.label: The Throat of the Sea
nodes.flavor: The Cartographer's recent charts explain nothing at all, except that every single one of them calls out the Gullet.
nodes.bridge: The Gullet is the only lead you have, and something down there is keeping a count. The way in runs through a channel sealed behind a Finndicate cipher.

scene.text: The Cartographer had a lot of charts. Old charts. Old routes. The Finndicate is a well-oiled operation. But his recent work still didn't explain anything.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: The waters he was trying to chart... I don't recognize them at all.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Well, there's definitely something interesting about all his charts. They all call out the Gullet.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: The Gullet, you say.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Yeah... this one says to always prepare extra for the Gullet.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: I'm not sure what to make of that. Don't tell me that's our only lead.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: That's our only lead.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Great.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Just read this other map... points at the Gullet too. It says: *"Don't mess up the count. The Gullet will swallow you whole. Our charts need to make it through."*

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Sounds inviting.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: I'm sure the Gullet will welcome us with open fins.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Set the sails, captain. We're in too deep now!

detail.description:
The Cartographer had charts by the locker-load. Old routes, old soundings, years of a well-oiled operation laid out in ink. None of it explains what he was doing lately, and Dole does not recognize the waters in his recent work at all.

One thing runs through every page of it. They all call out the Gullet. One says to always prepare extra for it. Another says not to mess up the count, because the Gullet will swallow you whole and the charts have to make it through. Nobody aboard can tell you what the count is. It is the only lead you have, and it is enough to sail on.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment VI
drops.sublabel: "Don't mess up the count. The Gullet will swallow you whole. Our charts need to make it through." Written in the margin of one of the Cartographer's own maps.

detail.dropsNote: One place named on every chart he owned, and a heading right down its throat.
detail.summary: The Cartographer's recent charts explained nothing except the Gullet, which every one of them called out. One warned not to mess up the count. It was the only lead you had, so you sailed down its throat.

nodes.label: The Wax Cipher
nodes.flavor: The mouth of the Gullet drowns any ship that reads the channel wrong. The only safe way in is sealed inside a Finndicate manifest, locked behind a row of wax cipher dials.
nodes.bridge: The seals line up, the manifest cracks, and the safe channel through the Gullet's teeth opens off your bow. So does a deduction at the foot of the page that nobody can account for.

puzzle.reveal:
The seals line up and the manifest cracks open. There's a thin lane of deep water through a throat of reef that'd gut any ship that guessed.

The rest of the page is an ordinary cargo list, right down to the last crate. Then, at the foot of it, a line nobody aboard can account for: a figure taken off the total, written in a different hand, with no reason given beside it. Whoever put it there never expected to be asked.

You've got the safe way into the Gullet now. Sail it.

detail.description: The Finndicate seals its headings behind wax cipher dials, rigged so no single turn ever gives the code away: turn one dial and the dials beside it turn with it. Line every seal to the brass index at once and the manifest reads true, the safe channel and all.

drops.label: 600 Nav XP
drops.sublabel: Cracking the manifest sharpens your navigation. No coin in it, just the safe heading.

detail.dropsNote: Turn the dials to line every seal to the index at once. Each turn also nudges the dials beside it. One-time, no cost, no fight.

nodes.label: A Throw of the Bones
nodes.flavor: A Finndicate freighter, half-swallowed and snagged on the reef, hold split open and bleeding cargo into the dark. How you plunder her is down to the bones.
nodes.bridge: The wreck slides off the reef behind you, picked over for whatever your throw was worth, and the deep harbor opens up ahead.

scene.text: Deep in the Gullet's throat, a Finndicate freighter hangs snagged on the reef, half-swallowed already.
Her hold's split wide, cargo bleeding out into the dark, and the whole wreck's one bad lurch from sliding off for good.
No time to be careful. Pick your play and roll the bones.

options.label: Skim the spill
options.description: Grab the cargo already loose in the water. Easy pickings, nothing fancy.
options.winText: Clean grab. Your hold's heavier and the wreck never even shifts.
options.missText: The current fights you the whole way, but you come up with a fistful anyway.

options.label: Pull the manifests
options.description: Leave the coin, dive for the freight charts. They're worth more than what's in the hold.
options.winText: You surface with the captain's charts dry and readable. Out here that's worth more than coin.
options.missText: Half the charts are pulp by the time you reach air. A few marks survive.

options.label: Crack the strongroom
options.description: Force the captain's strongroom before the wreck slides. All of it, or none of it.
options.winText: The strongroom gives all at once. You haul up more than the rest of the wreck put together.
options.missText: The wreck lurches off the reef and drags your grapples down with it. You cut loose with nothing but a lighter purse.

detail.description: A Finndicate freighter, snagged on the reef and half-swallowed, hold cracked wide and spilling cargo into the dark. She's one bad lurch from sliding off for good, so there's no being careful about it. Pick how you plunder her and throw the bones: a d20 plus a little of your Navigation, beat the mark to pull it off. Skim what's loose for easy coin, dive for the charts, or force the strongroom for everything she's got, knowing a bad throw on that one costs you.
detail.dropsNote: Pick one approach and roll once. The safe play always pays something; forcing the strongroom can cost you doubloons on a miss, and only opens to a captain who can cover the loss.
detail.summary: A half-sunk Finndicate freighter, plundered on a single throw of the bones. You made your play, the dice fell, and the wreck slid off the reef behind you.

nodes.label: The Sunken Cache
nodes.flavor: The Quartermaster has a shelf of gear deep inside the Gullet, far too well-stocked for water this far out. Two pieces on the counter, take one, leave the other.
nodes.bridge: The keeper knew your name before you gave it. You take your pick and try not to wonder too hard who told him you were coming.

scene.text: The channel drowns anything that guesses wrong. Past it, on a ledge of dead coral, there is a counter. Lamps lit. Stock laid out.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Captain. Good time through the teeth.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Long way past the danger line, this. You'd be amazed what gets delivered out here.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Fire or ice. Take one. Where you're going, you'll be glad of whichever you picked.

detail.description:
Deep in the Gullet, where no honest captain has charts, the Quartermaster is working a shelf of gear far too well-stocked for water this far out. He is already there. He always is. Two pieces of kit on the counter, take one, leave the other for good.

You grab what you came for and try not to think too hard about how he knew which water you were sailing. Whatever you take is yours to keep, ready to equip in your raid loadout with the rest of your kit.
detail.dropsNote: Pick one. Permanent, equippable, and you can't come back for the other.

nodes.label: A Sail in Your Lee
nodes.flavor: You hold at the mouth of the Gullet and watch the fog. Whether a friendly sail comes out of it is down to the mercy you showed back past the danger line.
nodes.bridge: Whatever answered your lee, the Gullet's throat is dead ahead now, and the captain who runs it is waiting at the bottom of it.

sceneUnmet.text: You hold at the Gullet's mouth and watch the fog for a friendly sail.
Out here you get back exactly what you gave, and you gave the cold water nothing.
Whatever's waiting down the throat, you'll meet it the way you came. Blind, and on your own keel.

sceneUnmet.speaker: Dole
sceneUnmet.text: No sail, then. Mercy compounds like interest. A pity you didn't invest.

sceneUnmet.speaker: Dole
sceneUnmet.text: So all we have is a word in a margin. Something down there keeps a count, and we are going to meet it without knowing whose it is.

scene.text: A cutter slides out of the fog and pulls in alongside you. No flag, but you know that hull.
The scouts you let go, way back past the danger line. Turns out the cold water remembers.

scene.speaker: A Freed Scout
scene.text: We owe you a deck, captain. We pay what we owe.

scene.speaker: A Freed Scout
scene.text: Every crew in the Gullet sails loaded. They've all got a shot in the pipe before the fight even starts.

scene.speaker: A Freed Scout
scene.text: They'll hit you on the first bell, before a slow captain's even found his range. Go in ready to take one.

scene.speaker: A Freed Scout
scene.text: And mind the count. Everything that goes down the throat gets weighed, and the Tollmaster takes his cut before anybody else sees a coin of it.
They hand across a strongbox and a folded chart, and slip back into the gray.
Richer, wiser, and not sailing in blind anymore. *The mercy paid.*

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: A crew that settles its debts in charts. I like them already.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: They're right about the first bell. Every hull in the Gullet opens loaded. Take on someone who sees it coming, and you open smarter.

detail.description: You hold at the mouth of the Gullet and watch the fog. Out here a captain gets back exactly what he gave, no more. If you cut those scouts loose back past the danger line, the cold water remembers, and a sail comes out of the gray to settle the debt with coin, charts, and a warning worth more than both. If you didn't, the fog stays empty and you go in the way you came.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment VII
drops.sublabel: "Out past the danger line, the only sail that comes back for you is one you let go."

detail.dropsNote: A payoff for an old mercy: the scouts you spared sail back with coin, charts, the only pre-fight intel in the game, and a name for whatever is doing the counting.
detail.summary: You held at the Gullet's mouth. What sailed out of the fog came down to the mercy you showed past the danger line, and the throat of the Gullet is dead ahead.

nodes.label: The Tollmaster's Cut
nodes.flavor: Down in the throat waits Tollmaster Spet, the barracuda who keeps the Finndicate's books. His quickest hulls sail loaded, a shot in the pipe before you've found your range.
nodes.bridge: Spet goes down and the Gullet drains dry. Three Finndicate captains on the seabed, a set of books nobody was ever meant to audit, and past here the cold water answers to a don even Spet would not name.

detail.description:
Tollmaster Spet keeps the Finndicate's books, and the Gullet is where the counting happens. Everything the outfit takes comes down this throat to be weighed against his page, which is a duller kind of power than a cannon and a much harder one to sink.

His barracuda crew take the First Cut: they open loaded and fire on the bell before a slow captain finds his range, and Spet himself opens with two. The whole toll line runs a harder cadence than anything you've fought, all volleys and double-taps. Equip his own drop and you can take the first cut right back.

drops.label: Chartmaker Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Spet's Primer
drops.sublabel: Raid item. 50% chance to start each raid fight with a cannonball already loaded, so you can fire on the opening bell.

drops.label: Tollmaster's Primer
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Always start each raid fight with a cannonball already loaded. The Tollmaster never waits to take his cut.

detail.dropsNote: One crate per Spet clear, rolled once and scaled by your Fortune. Every kill pays gold + Nav XP, and the run carries two Tide events between fights.

nodes.label: Challenge: The Tollmaster's Cut
nodes.flavor: The same loaded barracudas, drilled harder and angrier for the loss. Spet has had time to go back over the figures, and they still do not balance.

detail.description: The Tollmaster's whole toll line again, harder for the loss. The barracudas hit cleaner, Spet's doubled opener bites deeper, and every hull still fires first. He is not out here for the cargo this time. Crack his crate this run and his own Primer rolls at twice the rate.

drops.label: Chartmaker Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Spet's Primer
drops.sublabel: Raid item. 50% chance to start each raid fight with a cannonball already loaded, so you can fire on the opening bell.

drops.label: Tollmaster's Primer
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Always start each raid fight with a cannonball already loaded. The Tollmaster never waits to take his cut.

detail.dropsNote: Every kill pays more, the clear bonus is steeper, and the legendary Tollmaster's Primer rolls at double the normal rate.

nodes.label: Between Watches
nodes.flavor: The Tollmaster is under and his books are open. Before the next heading, the crew reads where all that coin was actually going.
nodes.bridge: The rest never lasts. Spet's own papers name where every sealed crate ended up: the Coffers, out in the northeastern seas.

scene.text: You've brought down the Tollmaster. And with it, the Finndicate's finances will have a gaping hole.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Spet's accounting only confirms what we know. They've been on a spending spree.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: That's why they've been pillaging and plundering. They're hungry for doubloons to fuel their purchases.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Spet counted the coin, but the doubloons still went past him.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: I remember seeing this on one of the Cartographer's maps too. Past the Gullet... everything gets dumped into something known as the *Coffers*.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Coffers? Guess we'll need to bring them some coff drops.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Anyways... Dole is right. Spet's own accounting documents show that anything signed and sealed by him gets sent over there.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: We've got a heading. It's gonna be out in the northeastern seas.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Rest up captain, we've got a long way to sail.
The next task looms large. But you know it's better to rest and be ready than to dive in. Right?

detail.description:
The Gullet is mud and the Tollmaster is under it, which leaves a gaping hole in the Finndicate's finances and their accounting lying wide open.

Spet's books confirm what the crew already suspected: the outfit has been on a spending spree, and all that pillaging was only ever fuel for it. The coin never stopped with Spet either. Anything he signed and sealed went on somewhere else, to a place the Cartographer's maps named as well. The Coffers, out in the northeastern seas. Rest up. It is a long way to sail.
detail.summary: With the Tollmaster under, his books named where every sealed crate went. The Finndicate has been spending everything it steals, and all of it ends up in the Coffers, out in the northeastern seas.

nodes.label: Captain's Choice
nodes.flavor: Three Finndicate captains on the seabed and the Gullet drained dry. Time to decide what your name stands for where the coin sleeps.

detail.description: You read the Cartographer's seas, cracked the Gullet's cipher, and put its collector under. Pick a class for the northeastern water ahead. Once it's chosen it stays with you for every raid from here on, stacking with the captain you already are.
detail.dropsNote: Deepen the class you already sail (a Mark II that stacks on top of it) or branch into a fresh one. It stays with you for good, barring the single refit the end of the campaign buys you.

nodes.label: Where the Coin Sleeps
nodes.flavor: Spet weighed everything the Gullet swallowed and kept none of it. His manifests all point the same way, to a harbor where the Finndicate's coin gets traded and divided.
nodes.bridge: The Coffers is where the Finndicate's money is tracked and divided, and you are closer to its inner workings than anyone has been. The only ways in are a blockade or a bribe.

scene.text: The Coffers. Seems like a place for the Finndicate elite. Even the air smells rich.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: It's a whole exchange out here. Everything must get traded at the harbor.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: So all the funds get tracked and then divvied up here?

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Seems like it. I feel like we're on a fast track to the real inner workings of the Finndicate now.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Looks like our reputation hasn't caught up to us yet... but before long they'll know of what we did.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Oh I know what you've all done.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Who...!

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: At ease, captains. Laz. I'm here looking to infiltrate Finndicate operations. They took down my family business.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: I've worked peacefully for years as a retired captain. They started pillaging our businesses for no reason. I managed to track down one of their merchant ships and have been following ever since.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: I came here once before to ask them why. They wrote me into the books as a debt, closed the account, and left me in this water. I'm the one entry they got wrong.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Not to sound creepy. But they've mentioned a motley crew going around taking down pieces of their operation one at a time. Their description... was accurate.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: ...And we just trust this?

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: We did for you.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Trust me or not, having eavesdropped on their merchant ships, I know my way around the harbor a bit now. I'm sure I'd be a valuable resource for your team.
Laz joins the party. He is now recruitable in your crew rolls.

detail.description:
Every manifest off Spet's deck points the same way: past the Gullet to a harbor the honest charts leave blank. The Coffers is the Finndicate's own exchange, where everything the outfit takes is traded, tracked and divided, and the air smells of how well that has been going.

Your reputation has not reached the place yet, which will not last. Laz found you on the way in: a retired captain the Finndicate pillaged out of his family business, who came here once to ask why and was written into their books as a debt, closed out, and left in the water. He has been following their merchant ships ever since, and he knows his way around the harbor. The only ways through its door are a blockade or a bribe.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment VIII
drops.sublabel: "Everything gets traded at the harbor. The funds get tracked here, and divided here."

detail.dropsNote: An exchange with a name at last, and two ways through its door.
detail.summary: Spet's manifests led you to the Coffers, the exchange where the Finndicate's coin is tracked and divided. Laz found you there: they ruined his family business, then closed his account and left him in this water. The way in is a blockade or a bribe.

nodes.label: The Harbor Gate
nodes.flavor: A barred gate stands across the channel into the Coffers. Blow it apart with one good cannon shot, or pay to be waved through.
nodes.bridge: The gate's behind you in pieces. Past it the harbor wall still stands, and a boom-chain across the last of the channel.

detail.description: One locked gate stands between you and the Coffers. Fire a single cannon shot at it: hit hard enough and it blows open for free. Come up short and you limp through under fire, and the repairs cost you 20,000 doubloons. Or skip the shot and just pay the dockmaster 10,000 to wave you in.
detail.dropsNote: Fire one shot and deal 40+ damage to pass for free, or pay 10,000 to skip it. A missed shot costs 20,000 in repairs.

nodes.label: The Signal Maze
nodes.flavor: The way past the harbor wall is to light the smugglers' own signal-lens, and the lantern that feeds it fires its beam through a maze of mirrors the market keeps deliberately crooked.
nodes.bridge: The lens flares green and the boom-chain drops into the water. The harbor fleet is dead ahead now.

puzzle.reveal:
The beam lands true on the lens and the whole signal flares green. Out past the wall, the harbor boom-chain groans down into the water.

The way in is open. The fleet is waiting.

detail.description: The market keeps its harbor-lantern fed through a maze of mirror-tiles set deliberately crooked, so no stranger can light the signal that drops the boom-chain. Turn the mirrors to bend the lantern's beam around the pillars and through every signal-lens at once.

drops.label: 650 Nav XP
drops.sublabel: Lighting the signal sharpens your navigation. No coin in it, just the way through.

detail.dropsNote: Plan one beam path through all three lenses, then fire. You get a limited number of fires before the mirrors reset. One-time, no cost, no fight.

nodes.label: The Last Cache
nodes.flavor: The Quartermaster's Cache keeps a stall even here, deep in the Coffers. The keeper waves you over, all smiles, and lays out two cuts of rigging. Take one.
nodes.bridge: New rig lashed on, and the market's war-fleet dead ahead. Whatever the keeper's grinning about, it'll keep till the guns are quiet.

scene.text: A stall in the drowned heart of the market, lit and stocked, and the keeper already waving you over.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: There you are. I was starting to wonder.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Rigging today. Crow's nest or trade winds. One sees further, one gets you there sooner.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Go on in, captain. I'll still be here after.

detail.description:
Even here, in the drowned heart of the market, the Quartermaster's Cache keeps a stall. The same shady supplier that's kitted you out since the coast. The keeper's all smiles today, a shade too glad to see you. He lays two cuts of ship's rigging on the counter: a crow's-nest set that sharpens your eye, or trade-wind canvas that keeps your guns fed. Pick one. The other rolls back under the counter.

Whatever you take is yours to keep, ready to equip in your raid loadout.
detail.dropsNote: Pick one rig. Permanent, equippable, and you can't come back for the other.

nodes.label: The Keeper's Smile
nodes.flavor: The Quartermaster is too glad to see you and too sure of your picks. He gives every captain who sails these shores a pick, and he likes to watch how far they get.
nodes.bridge: The crew talked themselves out of it and the war-fleet turned to meet you. Whatever the keeper is playing at, it keeps until the guns are quiet.

scene.text: You re-arm at the Quartermaster's Cache. The same stall that's kitted you since the coast.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Good pick! I'd have steered you to it myself.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Every captain who sails these shores gets a pick from me. I love to see how far they get.
The way he says it puts a cold coin in your gut.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Speaking of who we shouldn't trust... I don't like the Quartermaster.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Free is never really free... is it.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Hey we take what we can get. Who knows what dangers lie ahead.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Whoever he is, I sure hope he isn't Finndicate scum.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Wonder why he would be equipping us if he were.
The crew shrugs it off. You're sure it's fine, right?

detail.description:
You re-arm at the Quartermaster's Cache one last time, and the keeper is friendlier than any fair trade explains. He gives every captain who sails these shores a pick, he says, and he likes to watch how far they get.

The crew argue about him on the way out and talk themselves back down. Kat does not trust a gift. Doby says free is never free. Mako will take what is going. Laz, who the Finndicate wrote off once already, says out loud that he hopes the keeper is not one of theirs, and nobody has an answer for why a Finndicate keeper would be arming you. So they let it go, and the war-fleet is already turning.

drops.label: Overheard at the Counter
drops.sublabel: "Every captain who sails these shores gets a pick from me. I love to see how far they get."

detail.dropsNote: A last word from the Quartermaster before the fleet. Whatever he means by it, it waits till the guns are quiet.
detail.summary: The Quartermaster was friendlier than any fair trade explains, saying he gives every captain a pick and likes to watch how far they get. The crew talked themselves out of suspecting him, and the war-fleet turned to meet you.

nodes.label: The Harbor Fleet
nodes.flavor: The Finndicate's coffers keep a war-fleet, and Admiral Ruse has never lost a hull. His gunners fly false colors on every shot, so you never know which gun is the one that's loaded.
nodes.bridge: Admiral Ruse's fleet is wreckage on the harbor floor, and the Finndicate's coffers lie open. Whatever their mission is, it's paid for in there.

detail.description: The Coffers' war-fleet and its admiral, Ruse, who has never lost a ship. His crews fight under false colors: decoy gun-bands strewn across your aim so you can't tell the live shot from the feint. The biggest hulls you've faced yet, and Ruse rises again when you think you've sunk him.

drops.label: Coffers Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Tell-Tale Glass
drops.sublabel: Raid item. When an enemy would dodge your shot, 20% chance to read the feint and land it anyway.

drops.label: Admiral's Eye
drops.sublabel: Raid item. When an enemy would dodge your shot, 35% chance to read the feint and land it anyway.

detail.dropsNote: One crate per clear, rolled once and scaled by your Fortune. Every kill pays gold + Nav XP, and the run carries two stronger Tide events between fights.

nodes.label: Challenge: The Harbor Fleet
nodes.flavor: The same fleet, drilled harder and flying meaner colors. Admiral Ruse doesn't lose his wall twice.

detail.description: The harbor fleet again, harder for the loss. More HP, sharper guns, the same wall of false colors, and the admiral's phase 2 bites deeper. The chase rewards roll richer for the trouble.

drops.label: Coffers Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Tell-Tale Glass
drops.sublabel: Raid item. When an enemy would dodge your shot, 20% chance to read the feint and land it anyway.

drops.label: Admiral's Eye
drops.sublabel: Raid item. When an enemy would dodge your shot, 35% chance to read the feint and land it anyway.

detail.dropsNote: Every kill pays more and the clear bonus is steeper than the normal run.

nodes.label: The Cache Turns
nodes.flavor: You put in at the Quartermaster's Cache to re-arm, the same shady stall that's kitted you out since the coast. This time the keeper's smiling, and the guns behind the counter are pointed your way.
nodes.bridge: The Cache was theirs the whole time. Every blade they sold you was a leash, and the keeper answers to a name you've not heard yet: Don Finleone.

scene.text: You put in at the Quartermaster's Cache to re-arm. Same stall that's kitted you out since the coast.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Captain. Knew you'd wash up here eventually. They all do.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Every hook, every cannon, every clever little trick. You bought it all off me.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: The Cache was *never neutral*, captain. There's no such thing out here.
The guns behind the counter swing your way. The shelves you've trusted since the coast were *Finndicate all along*.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: I armed you because they let me. And whatever I sold you, *I can take back*.

detail.description: The Quartermaster's Cache, the shady stall that's armed you since the coast, sits in the heart of the Coffers, and the keeper's been expecting you. It was a Finndicate front the whole time. Every piece of kit you bought was a leash, and the merchant who sold it can yank it back. He answers to the don who runs the market, the first time you hear the name: Don Finleone.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment IX
drops.sublabel: "The one who armed you and the one hunting you were always the same."

detail.dropsNote: The betrayal at the heart of the Coffers: the shop was theirs, and it names the don above it.
detail.summary: The Quartermaster's Cache, the stall that armed you since the coast, was a Finndicate front all along. The keeper turned his guns on you, and named the don he answers to: Don Finleone.

nodes.label: Crack the Strongbox
nodes.flavor: The keeper's guns are out and his floor's gone to chaos. Bolted to the counting-house planks sits a strongbox fat with the day's take, and his muscle is closing fast. Time for exactly one grab.
nodes.bridge: Strongbox settled one way or the other, you shove deeper into the market, toward the light-lock that bars his vault.

scene.text: The moment the keeper's guns come up, his counting-house turns into a riot.
Clerks bolt, coin scatters underfoot, and his hired muscle starts shoving through the crowd toward you.
Bolted to the planks by the scales sits a strongbox, lid still warm from the day's counting.
You'll get one grab at it before they reach you. Pick your play and be quick.

options.label: Skim the till
options.description: Sweep the loose coin off the counter and keep moving. Easy, safe, and a little beneath a strongbox like that.
options.winText: You come away with two fists of the market's coin and never break stride.
options.missText: Half of it spills as you grab, but a fair weight lands in your hold anyway.

options.label: Force the strongbox
options.description: Put a bar under the lid and lean on it before the muscle arrives. More coin, less time.
options.winText: The lid pops with a crack and you scoop the day's take clean into your hold.
options.missText: The lid gives late and you snatch what you can as the first of his muscle reaches you.

options.label: Blow the safe
options.description: Powder-charge the whole safe and take everything at once. All or nothing, and a bad light costs you.
options.winText: The charge blows the safe wide and you haul off more coin than the fleet outside was worth.
options.missText: The powder catches wrong, the blast throws you back empty-handed, and your own charge cost you a purse.

detail.description: The keeper's turned his guns on you and his counting-house has gone to a riot: clerks bolting, coin underfoot, his hired muscle shoving toward you through the crowd. Bolted to the planks by the scales sits a strongbox fat with the day's take. You get one grab before they reach you. Throw the bones on it: skim the loose till for safe coin, force the box for more, or powder-charge the whole safe for everything it holds, knowing a bad light costs you.
detail.dropsNote: Pick one grab and roll once. The safe play always pays; blowing the safe can cost you doubloons on a miss, and only opens to a captain who can cover the loss.

nodes.label: The Vault Beam
nodes.flavor: The Quartermaster's strongroom answers to a lock of light: a sunbeam channelled down through the market's roof, off a row of mirrors he can crook from behind his counter. Straighten them and the vault opens.
nodes.bridge: The beam strikes the vault-eye and the strongroom bars grind back. The keeper is cornered behind them now.

puzzle.reveal:
The beam threads the last mirror and strikes the vault-eye dead center. Deep in the iron, the strongroom bars grind back.

The Quartermaster's behind them, cornered, with nowhere left to run.

detail.description: The Quartermaster bars his strongroom behind a lock of light, a sunbeam bent down through a row of mirrors he keeps crooked from behind his counter. Turn the mirrors to thread the beam through all three vault-eyes at once and the bars slide back.

drops.label: 750 Nav XP
drops.sublabel: Picking the keeper's light-lock sharpens your navigation. No coin, just the way in.

detail.dropsNote: Plan one beam path through all three lenses, then fire. You get a limited number of fires before the mirrors reset. One-time, no cost, no fight.

nodes.label: The Ledger of Debts
nodes.flavor: The Quartermaster's vault isn't a strongroom. It's the back-stock of a shop, drowned and kept, and chained in the middle of it is a ledger naming every captain he ever armed and how each one sank.
nodes.bridge: You know now what the Cache really was. The Quartermaster's cornered against his own shelves, still smiling, and every debt in his book runs up to one name: Don Finleone.

scene.text: The bars grind back and the vault breathes out cold, coin-smelling air. It isn't a strongroom. It's a shop's back-stock, sunk to the bottom of the sea and kept dry.
Shelf on shelf of other captains' plunder, every piece tagged, sorted, and priced to sell back to whoever comes up next.
Chained to a stand in the heart of it, a ledger the size of a hatch cover. Every captain the Quartermaster ever armed, and beside each name, a note on how they sank.
Lost off the Shrouds. Drowned in the Gullet. Sold their own hull back a plank at a time. Debt cleared, debt cleared, debt cleared.
Your name's near the bottom, in fresh ink. The line for how you sank is still blank.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: Every account in that book closes the same way, captain, and every one settles up to the don. Finleone likes his ledgers tidy. Yours is the one line I have left open.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: I know this book. My name is a few pages up, and the line for how I sank was filled in long ago.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: They were wrong. I have read this ledger from the other side of it. Let me be the one to see his account closed the right way.

scene.speaker: The Quartermaster
scene.text: You think Finleone stocked these shelves? Somebody stocked *him*. Somebody who never once came down here to collect.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: He's stalling. Close the account.

detail.description: The vault opens not on a strongroom but on a shop's drowned back-stock: shelf on shelf of other captains' plunder, tagged and priced to be sold back to the next crew that comes up. Chained at its heart is the Quartermaster's ledger, naming every captain he ever armed and, beside each name, a note on how they sank. Your own name sits near the bottom in fresh ink, that note still blank. And every debt in the book runs up to one name: Don Finleone. Now you understand the Quartermaster's smile, and why he opened this fight by taking his own guns back off you.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment X
drops.sublabel: "He wrote down how every captain he armed would die. Mine is the only line he hasn't filled in."

detail.dropsNote: The truth of the Cache, and the name the Quartermaster answers to: Don Finleone. Whatever he sold you, he can take back.
detail.summary: Inside the vault you found the Quartermaster's ledger: every captain he ever armed, each with a note on how they sank, all running up to Don Finleone. Your name's in it, the note on your death still blank, and he means to take his guns back.

nodes.label: The Quartermaster
nodes.flavor: The keeper of the Cache fights the way he sells: he opens by taking back a piece of your own kit, then makes you buy your life off him one shot at a time.
nodes.bridge: The Quartermaster goes down under his own counter and the Cache's hold falls open for good. Every debt in that ledger settles at once, and the account runs up past him, to the don.

detail.description: The Quartermaster himself, behind the guns of the market he runs.
