He fights the way he trades, all misdirection: he floods the bay with false flares to foul your aim, and slips live shells in among them that you'll regret swatting. Read the real targets, intercept the rest, then put him under, through his reserve deck and all, to spill the Cache's hold.

drops.label: Coffers Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: War Drum
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Once per raid: beat the drum for a 40% chance to restore a random spent crew ability. Fires from the Special menu and does not cost your turn.

drops.label: Thunder Drum
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Once per raid: beat the drum to restore a random spent crew ability, guaranteed. Fires from the Special menu and does not cost your turn.

detail.dropsNote: One crate per clear, rolled once and scaled by your Fortune. He opens by reclaiming one of your equipped raid items for the whole fight. Two stronger Tide events between fights.

nodes.label: Challenge: The Quartermaster
nodes.flavor: The keeper again, angrier for the loss, and he reclaims more than you can spare. He does not get robbed twice.

detail.description: The Quartermaster's finale again, harder for the loss. More HP, sharper guns, the same opening theft and the same reserve-deck phase 2, all of it meaner. The chase rewards roll richer.

drops.label: Coffers Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: War Drum
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Once per raid: beat the drum for a 40% chance to restore a random spent crew ability. Fires from the Special menu and does not cost your turn.

drops.label: Thunder Drum
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Once per raid: beat the drum to restore a random spent crew ability, guaranteed. Fires from the Special menu and does not cost your turn.

detail.dropsNote: Every kill pays more and the clear bonus is steeper than the normal run.

nodes.label: Between Watches
nodes.flavor: The Quartermaster's ledgers spill and name the don at the top of it all. Then the Coffers burn low, and before the deepest water the crew takes a watch together, one navigator unable to quite settle.
nodes.bridge: You have the don's name now: Finleone, at the top of every ledger. The rest never lasts, and past the last of the Coffers' light the sea drops toward the seat he rules from.

scene.text: The Quartermaster's strongbox cracks, and the last of his ledgers spill across the deck. Not one of them argues with the others.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: I've been adding this up since the coast, and here's the sum. Pete fed Krust. Krust fed the Gullet. The Gullet fed this market. And every coin of it, all of it, runs up to one signature.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Don Finleone. A megalodon the sea was said to have swallowed and thought better of. He runs the Coffers, and the Coffers ran everything.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: The head of the whole Finndicate, and he sits at the bottom of the deepest water there is. I've wanted to bite something that size my whole life.
The Coffers burn low, the Quartermaster's counter down to kindling, and for the first time since the harbor gate the deck goes quiet.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: You say the loveliest things right before I have to stitch you back together. Sit down, the pair of you.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: I knew a captain once who thought he was the biggest thing in the water. The water disagreed. It always does, in the end.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Cut the head and the whole body falls. That's the plan, is it not, navigator?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: It is. It should even be true.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: There's a doubt in your voice.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: There's a margin in my notes I can't account for. A few sums that tie up to no name I have. But that's a worry for deeper water. Tonight, we won.
Past the last of the Coffers' light, the sea drops away toward the seat the don rules from. But that is tomorrow's heading.
Tonight the crew is whole, one hand heavier still, and the grog is cold.

detail.description: The Quartermaster's ledgers spill and settle the same way every time: up to one signature, Don Finleone, the megalodon who runs the Coffers and every Cache that feeds them. As far as any ledger in the market knows, he is the head of the Finndicate. Then the counter burns low and the crew takes a watch: Mako itching to bite something megalodon-sized, Kat threatening to stitch him for saying so, Laz grave over how big things end, and Dole unable to shake a margin in his notes that will not add up. A worry for deeper water. Tonight the crew is whole.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment XI
drops.sublabel: "Every debt in the market runs up to one name: Finleone. Every ledger down here calls him the head of the whole Finndicate."

detail.dropsNote: The don named at the top of every ledger, and the crew whole before the deep.
detail.summary: The Quartermaster's ledgers all ran up to Don Finleone, the megalodon who runs the Coffers and the whole Finndicate. Then the crew took a watch before the deepest water. Dole cannot quite settle a margin in his notes, but tonight the crew is whole.

nodes.label: Captain's Choice
nodes.flavor: The Coffers in ruins, the Quartermaster under, and a don's name at the top of every ledger. Time to set what your colors mean before the deepest water.

detail.description: You ran the harbor wall, faced the market's fleet, and put the Quartermaster under his own counter. Pick a class for the deep water where Finleone waits. It stays with you for every raid from here on, stacking with the captain you already are.
detail.dropsNote: Deepen the class you already sail or branch into a fresh one. It stays with you for good, barring the single refit the end of the campaign buys you.

nodes.label: The Deepest Water
nodes.flavor: The Coffers burn behind you and every ledger points one way: down, past the last sounding on any chart, to the seat Don Finleone rules from. The deepest water there is. And nothing waits past it.
nodes.bridge: The heading is set for the don's own water. And the Quartermaster's seized stock sails with you. A vault of everything he never sold you.

scene.text: The Coffers burn low behind you, and the sea ahead simply runs out of chart. Past the last sounding, past the last named reef, the water only goes down.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: The last fathom. I was born in water like this, small fry. Black, and cold, and patient. It is the one part of the sea I have ever been afraid of.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Good. Fear is how an old whale stays an old whale. Take us down.
You are not the only sail bound for the edge of the chart. One you do not know has been holding your distance since the Coffers, matching you turn for turn.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Don Finleone. The one bounty in this whole sea nobody's fool enough to chase. And here you are, sailing off the last sounding to do exactly that.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: I do love a captain with no sense of self-preservation. It's the only kind worth following.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Mira. I hunt the marks the smart money leaves alone. When you crew up for the deepest water, put my name down. I want a good seat for this one.
She lets her sail settle in beside yours like the hunt's already decided.

detail.description: Past the Coffers there is no more market, no more middlemen, no more names between you and the don. The chase runs out of chart here: Don Finleone's seat lies in the deepest water there is, and the crew have taken to calling it the last fathom. The depth past which nothing comes back up. Set the heading.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment XII
drops.sublabel: "Past the last sounding the water only goes down. So that's where we go."

detail.dropsNote: The final chapter opens. The heading is set for the deepest water.
detail.summary: The heading is set past the last sounding on any chart. For the deepest water there is, and the don who rules it. The final chapter has begun.

nodes.label: The Powder Hold
nodes.flavor: The don's water doesn't forgive a loose hold. Every powder crate stows on its mark before the blockade, or the first broadside does the stowing for you.
nodes.bridge: The hold is stowed tight and the guns are fed. Ahead: the blockade, and the don’s right fin who runs it.

puzzle.reveal:
The hold sits trim and the powder is dry.
Past the next swell: the blockade line, and Sal Brackwater who holds it.

detail.description: Three holds of powder crates, and every crate has a marked square it must sit on before the blockade. Crates shove, they never pull, so a crate pushed into a corner stays there. Stow all three holds within the move budget; run out of moves and the hold resets.
detail.dropsNote: Solving the hold pays Nav XP. The budget resets the room, never the run. Read the hold before you shove.

nodes.label: The Muster
nodes.flavor: A cutter comes alongside before the line will part, and a clerk with a wet ledger counts your crew like livestock. He is not looking for guns. He is looking for hands that can do something when the shooting starts.
nodes.bridge: The clerk closes his ledger, unimpressed but satisfied. The line parts.

detail.description:
The don's clerk comes aboard to count your crew before the line will part. He is not counting guns.

What is past this point cannot be out-shot. Sal Brackwater will take your hull in his teeth and roll, and the ONLY thing that stops it is a crew ability. Not a dodge. Not a good shot. A crew member who can get between you and the blow.

Bring hands who can do something, or the clerk sends you home.
detail.dropsNote: No cost and no fight. Bring the right crew and the line parts.
detail.summary: The don's clerk counted your crew and found hands worth letting through.

nodes.label: The Quartermaster's Ghost
nodes.flavor: The gun-deck is exactly as he left it, and so is he. The drowned keep better books than the living, and he never did stop counting what you owe.
nodes.bridge: The ghost keeps his counter open. Whatever you left in the Caches, and whatever you have melted down since, he still has it, and he will keep handing it back for as long as you keep putting him down.
nodes.gateLockNote: Beat The Quartermaster on Challenge first. Open his raid card and pick Challenge.

detail.description:
He is holding every Cache item you left behind, and every one you forged away.

50% DROP CHANCE EVERY CLEAR. Half your runs pay a Cache item, and it is split evenly across the ones you still need, so the last one is exactly as likely as the first was. Crew Fortune raises it, up to double. Run him as often as you like.

HE FIGHTS WITH THEM. Your fire, your ice, your sights, your plating, your bearings, all turned on you. Every item you take back is one he can never use again.

FOUR BARS, THREE CHECKS. He patches his hull with your plating, lights your fire-shot, and calls a shot down your own sights. Answer each with a CREW ABILITY.

drops.label: Quartermaster's Anchor
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Once per raid, a killing blow leaves you at 1 HP instead of sinking. Raids only, never skirmishes.

drops.label: Navigator's Compass
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Adds 20% of your Savvy to your turn-order roll, so you strike first more often.

drops.label: Gunner's Sight
drops.sublabel: Raid item. +15% damage on critical hits, but non-critical shots hit for 15% less. A trade for the steady-handed.

drops.label: Reinforced Hull
drops.sublabel: Raid item. +15% max HP at the start of every raid. Heavier strakes, slower to sink.

drops.label: Incendiary Cannonball
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Each hit has a 15% chance to set the enemy ablaze, burning them for 2 turns (damage scaled to the hit that lit them).

drops.label: Frozen Cannonball
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Each hit has a 15% chance to freeze the enemy solid, making them lose their next turn.

drops.label: Crow's-Nest Rigging
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Each of your normal hits has a 15% chance to become a critical hit for much bigger damage.

drops.label: Trade-Wind Sails
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Each time you reload, a 15% chance to load 2 cannonballs at once instead of 1.

detail.dropsNote: 50% chance of a Cache item every clear, spread evenly over the ones you do not currently have. Crew Fortune raises it.
detail.summary: The Quartermaster died still holding every Cache item you passed up, and he collects the ones you forge away too. Half your runs he hands one back, and you can run him as often as you like.

nodes.label: The Thing on the Bar
nodes.flavor: Something long and low lies on the drowned bar, where the last sunken channel spills over into the deep. The lookout calls it a fallen spar and goes back to his knots. It is still there an hour later, in exactly the same place, and it has not moved once.
nodes.bridge: The spar was not a spar. It was waiting, and it was in no hurry at all.

scene.text: The lookout calls a spar on the drowned bar at the lip of the drop. Half-sunk, barnacled, settled off some wreck down the sunken channel. Nobody looks twice.
An hour on, the bosun notices it is still there. Same bar. Same angle. The tide has moved a foot and a half in that time and the spar *has not moved at all*.
A spar drifts. A spar rolls with the water. This one is lying against the pull of the deep.
You watch it for a long minute. It does not move. Nothing about it moves. Then, without any part of it seeming to turn, you are aware that *it is facing you*.
The blockade line is ahead. So is he. Remember this: when the water goes flat and nothing at all is happening, that is not nothing happening. *That is him deciding.*

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: A thing that doesn't move is a thing that's already decided you're food. I've pulled too many crews off too many decks not to know the look. Don't blink first, captain.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: A thing that lies perfectly still until the moment it doesn't. I know the type. I'm the type.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: So when the water goes flat, don't wait to see what he decides. Make him answer what you decide instead.

detail.description:
A spar on the drowned bar that does not drift, does not roll, and does not move with the tide. Watch it long enough and you understand it is not wreckage. It is waiting.

Remember the shape of it: when the water goes flat and nothing seems to be happening, that is Sal deciding.
detail.dropsNote: The tell, learned for free instead of the hard way.
detail.summary: A spar on the drowned bar that never drifted. It was not a spar, and it had been watching for some time.

nodes.label: The Blockade
nodes.flavor: Don Finleone's blockade line, and the thing that holds it: Sal Brackwater, who has not moved in an hour and is not going to until it matters. Every hull rides behind a cold-light barrier, every magazine runs four deep, and his line fights dirtier than any market ever did.
nodes.bridge: The blockade breaks and Sal Brackwater goes under it. The way to the don's own water lies open. And his books ride in your hold.

detail.description:
The don's escort fleet, and it does not fight like anything you have met.

Every hull rides behind a barrier, so your opening shots buy nothing but broken plating. Their magazines run four deep, and a ship that has been firing all round is never as empty as you would like. And they fight dirty: nets for your rudder, chain-shot for your guns, cracker rounds for your seams, and a gag order for your crew.

At the center of the line, something long and low lies in the water and does not move.

drops.label: Last Fathom Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Chain-Shot Rack
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Landed hits have a 25% chance to fire a spread that tears both rigging and plating. WEAKENED: it deals 20% less damage. CORRODED: its barrier takes 30% more damage. Both for 2 rounds. Sal Brackwater's own answer, turned back on the Finndicate.

drops.label: Brackwater Rack
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Landed hits have a 35% chance to fire a spread of scrap iron. WEAKENED: it deals 20% less damage. CORRODED: its barrier takes 30% more damage. FEEBLE: it takes 20% more damage. All three, for 2 rounds. Sal's own rack, hauled off his wreck and turned around.

detail.dropsNote: One crate per clear, rolled once and scaled by your Fortune. The Chain-Shot Rack is the signature chase. Turn their own Weaken back on them. Two stronger Tide events between fights.

nodes.label: Challenge: The Blockade
nodes.flavor: The blockade re-forms, heavier at every post. Sal Brackwater does not hold a line twice. He buries it.

detail.description: The blockade again, and it has learned. Every ship is tougher, every barrier thicker, and Sal rolls harder. Same rules, none of the mercy. The chase rewards roll richer for it.

drops.label: Last Fathom Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Chain-Shot Rack
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Landed hits have a 25% chance to fire a spread that tears both rigging and plating. WEAKENED: it deals 20% less damage. CORRODED: its barrier takes 30% more damage. Both for 2 rounds. Sal Brackwater's own answer, turned back on the Finndicate.

drops.label: Brackwater Rack
drops.sublabel: Raid item. Landed hits have a 35% chance to fire a spread of scrap iron. WEAKENED: it deals 20% less damage. CORRODED: its barrier takes 30% more damage. FEEBLE: it takes 20% more damage. All three, for 2 rounds. Sal's own rack, hauled off his wreck and turned around.

detail.dropsNote: Every kill pays more and the clear bonus is steeper than the normal run.

nodes.label: A Sixth Crew Slot
nodes.flavor: He came apart along the grain, the way he tore everything else apart, and his hull showed you its bones on the way down. Six berths framed into a deck that had no business carrying more than five. Nobody does that by accident.
nodes.bridge: The plans are in your chart locker and your carpenters have stopped arguing about whether it can be done. Six, if you want to pay for it.

detail.description:
Your ship carries FIVE crew. Sal's carried six, and when he broke open you finally saw how: the deck is framed wrong on purpose, load taken where no shipwright would put it. The plans were still in his locker, salted and legible, and you took them.

Your own carpenters can read them. Cut open the hull, re-frame it, and you sail with a SIXTH CREW SLOT: one more crew aboard, permanently, on every raid and every voyage.

It costs a fortune. Take the plans to your shipwrights in Manage Ship when you are ready to pay for it.
detail.dropsNote: A permanent sixth crew slot, on raids and voyages both. Bought once in Manage Ship, and it never comes off.
detail.summary: Sal's hull was framed for six, and you took the plans off the wreck. Your own shipwrights can cut a SIXTH CREW SLOT into your deck for a fortune: one more crew aboard, on every raid and voyage, permanently. Buy it in Manage Ship.

nodes.label: The Crooked Ledger
nodes.flavor: Sal Brackwater's strongroom gives up the don's own accounts, every column in his own hand. Read them and the debts all run down into one pocket. Past one last lock, Don Finleone is waiting on his throne.
nodes.bridge: The books settle the argument: the don sits at the top of it all. One last lock, and then his throne.

scene.text: The strongroom door gives with a groan, and Sal Brackwater's last secret spills out across the deck: ledgers stacked to the beam, every one filled in the same close, careful hand.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Give me a moment with these. Rates, tithes, tolls, drowned debts... and every column, every last one, runs down into the same pocket.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Whose pocket?

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: One guess, and you won't need it. There's only ever been one name at the top of this water.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Finleone. Felt it in my gut a hundred leagues back. Another thing to hold it in his own ink, though.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Forty years I've watched good captains drown arguing whose fault the sea was. The don kept the answer in a ledger the whole time.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Now that is a curiosity. There's a second hand in these margins, and it isn't his. Older. Finer. Initials a few odd sums that tie to no account I can find anywhere in the book.
One letter, looped small and patient at the bottom of a column, over and over, page after page.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Dead partner. Some debt he never troubled to close. Every old crook keeps a ghost or two in his columns, and none of them ever collect.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Leave it lie. We have a don to put in the ground.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Then the books are done talking. He's at the end of them, on his throne, waiting. Let us go settle the account in person.

detail.description: Sal Brackwater's strongroom gave up the don's ledgers, every column in Finleone's own hand. The debts all run down into one pocket: his. Dole finds one margin in an older hand nobody can place, initialling a few odd sums that tie to nothing. A dead partner's ghost, most like. Nothing between you and the throne now but one last lock.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment XIII
drops.sublabel: "Every debt runs up to Finleone, and every book agrees he is the head of it. There is one margin that does not. The throne is ahead."

detail.dropsNote: The don's whole empire, balanced to the coin in his own careful hand.
detail.summary: Sal Brackwater's strongroom gave up the don's ledgers. Every column runs down into one pocket: Finleone's. The books settle it in his own hand, and one last lock is all that stands between you and his throne.

nodes.label: The Throne Gates
nodes.flavor: The don's gate is one great lock: iron bars over iron bars, and a single gold bolt that only runs when every tumbler stands clear. Nobody knocks.
nodes.bridge: The last tumbler throws and the gates swing on silence. Past them: the deepest water there is, and the don sitting in it.

puzzle.reveal:
The bolt runs free and the gates part.
No horns, no guns. The don knew you were coming the whole way down.

detail.description: Three tumblers, each a lattice of iron bars over one gold bolt. Bars slide along their grooves, never sideways, and the bolt only runs when its whole row stands clear to the edge. Throw all three within the slide budget; run out and the tumbler resets to its first set.
detail.dropsNote: Throwing the gate pays Nav XP. The budget resets the tumbler, never the gate. Read the bars before you slide.

nodes.label: The Drowned Court
nodes.flavor: The gates open on the deepest water there is, and the don's court rides at anchor around one lit flagship. Six apex killers arrayed like courtiers, the most dangerous crew in the sea, and the biggest name in it sitting still at the center of them.
nodes.bridge: The court knows your name now. His right hand has promised, in his voice, that you will not leave this water. Past him, the aisle to the throne stands open.

scene.text: The last gate swings on silence and you slip into the don's own black water. No horns. No warning shot. Just the pressure of the deep and one lit flagship far ahead, ringed by its court.
Six hulls ride at anchor around it, arrayed like courtiers around a throne. Each flies the shark colors. Each, on any other water, would have been the thing you came to sink.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Look at them. A Render. A Reaper. The don's own Closer, by the scars on that one. Every single one a bounty I'd have crossed an ocean for on its own. And they're only the DOOR.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: In a long life on this water I've never seen them gathered in one place. Every hull there is a shark whole fleets tell stories about to frighten one another quiet. The don didn't hire this court. He collected it. The deadliest thing each dark corner of the sea ever spat out, all anchored in one room.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Six of the biggest killers in the sea, and one enormous one at the back of the room. Do you have any idea how long I've wanted a table set like this?

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Mako. That's not a table. That's the thing that eats the table, and everyone still sitting at it.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: The Closer there has put down more captains than the other five combined, and every one of those five is an apex the whole trade gave up trying to touch. Which makes it curious that he's the one peeling off the line to greet us. A court doesn't send its deadliest just to say hello.
One hull peels from the ring, all cold precision, and stops across your bow. Close enough to read the old scars crossing his plating like a ledger of every captain he has closed.

scene.speaker: The Closer
scene.text: The don sends his regards, little captain. He has read your whole story. The barnacle. The old hauler. The market. The thing on the bar. A tidy little climb.

scene.speaker: The Closer
scene.text: He wanted you to hear it from me, since I keep his accounts: you will not leave this water. The line for how you sink is already written, in his own hand. You are simply the last to read it.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: That's the same voice that read me my debt, a lifetime ago, in this exact water. Calm. Certain. Counting me closed before I had drawn a breath to argue.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: It was wrong about me. I am still here.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Then let it be wrong twice. The court can talk all it likes. We came to answer.
The Closer holds a moment longer, as if offering you the chance to turn. You do not. He slides back into the ring, and the court parts, an aisle of guns opening straight to the throne.

detail.description: The don's court rides at anchor around his lit flagship: six shark-captains, and not one a common hull. Every one is an apex killer the whole trade long ago gave up trying to touch. The deadliest crew in the sea, hand-picked by the don. His right hand, the Closer, glides out to read you his terms: he has watched your whole climb, found it quaint, and already written the line for how you sink. Then the court parts, and the aisle to the throne opens.

drops.label: The Closer's Terms
drops.sublabel: "The line for how you sink is already written, in his own hand. You are simply the last to read it."

detail.dropsNote: The don's court, named and arrayed. And his mouthpiece's promise, in his voice, that you will not leave this water.
detail.summary: Past the gates, the don's court parted for you. But not before his consigliere promised, in his name, that you would not leave this water.

nodes.label: The Last Muster
nodes.flavor: The court parts, but one hull holds the aisle: the don's doorman, The Gnash, counting your deck before it lets you through. The don does not admit a half-crewed deck to his table.
nodes.bridge: The Gnash slides aside, unimpressed. Nothing stands between you and the throne now but open water.

detail.description:
The Gnash blocks the aisle and reads your deck. What waits at the throne answers to nothing but the right hand at the right moment: a brace or a shield when the whole court fires as one, a mender when the don's jaws find your hull, and someone who can jam or blast him out of a dive. Bring hands for all three, or the doorman turns you back.

This is the fight the Sixth Berth was built for. Field your whole crew.
detail.dropsNote: No cost and no fight. Bring a crew that can answer the don's court, and the aisle opens.
detail.summary: The don's doorman counted your crew and found hands enough to face the throne.

nodes.label: Within Hail
nodes.flavor: The aisle of guns opens onto the throne, and for the first time the don deigns to speak, almost impressed you climbed the whole ladder only to learn where it ends. Then he goes still, and the whole black sea goes still with him.
nodes.bridge: The don has said his piece: you will not beat him, nothing in his water ever has. The sea lies flat as a held breath. There is nothing left between you and the biggest name in it.

scene.text: You take the aisle. The court holds its fire and its formation, every gun tracking you in, and the lit flagship at the end grows from a lantern to a leviathan.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Bigger than the stories. Bigger than the Cartographer swore anything in this sea could get. I didn't think I'd ever be the small one at a table.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Everything ran up to him. Every debt, every drowned captain, every clever little sum I read off a dead captain's ledger. And here he is at the bottom of it all, exactly where the numbers said he'd be. I do hate being right about a monster.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Hold your nerve. This is the mark no one in the trade will touch. Which means when he goes down, it's us who put him there. And no one else in the whole sea gets to say it.
Close enough to hail now, and the don, who has not stirred for the whole descent, finally lifts his vast head and regards you the way you would look at a coin you have already spent.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: All this way. Past my hauler, my market, my whole drowned family. I confess I am almost impressed, little captain.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: Almost. You have climbed the entire ladder to learn the one thing every captain learns too late: the ladder ends in a mouth. You will not beat me. Nothing in this water ever has. But come. Let me see how you sink.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Big words, for a fish.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: Let him talk. The drowned always sound certain, right up until the water disagrees. And it always does, in the end.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: You have the whole crew at your back and the biggest name in the sea in front of you. I've waited a long life to see a captain stand here. Take him.
Then the don falls still, stiller than a thing that size has any right to hold, and the court falls still with him. The whole black water holds its breath.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Steady. Something this old only goes quiet right before it moves.

detail.description: The aisle opens onto the throne, and the don finally deigns to speak. Almost impressed you climbed the whole ladder, only to learn it ends in a mouth. He tells you plainly you will not beat him; nothing in his water ever has. Then he goes still, and the whole black sea goes still with him.

drops.label: The Don's Word
drops.sublabel: "You have climbed the entire ladder to learn the one thing every captain learns too late: the ladder ends in a mouth."

detail.dropsNote: The don's own promise, delivered face to face: you will not beat him. Time to find out.
detail.summary: Within hail of the throne, the don spoke: you will not beat him, nothing in his water ever has. Then he went still, and so did the sea.

nodes.label: Don Finleone
nodes.flavor: The court rides at anchor and the don sits still at the center of it, done talking. Every hull here carries a trick you haven't been hit with yet. And the don carries all of them.
nodes.bridge: The court is drowned and the don with it. The Finndicate dies here, on its own throne, in its own black water. The biggest name in the sea, finally answered for.

detail.description: The don's own court, and every hull in it fights with a new kind of dirty. Watch their cannonball pips: a FULL, glowing battery means an ULTIMATE is primed. Burn their charges down, shield, or brace before it empties into you. And their specials strike your AIM BAR itself: false gold you must not lock, plated locks that take two taps, squalls that gust your needle mid-sweep. Don Finleone waits at the center. And what rises when his mask drops is nothing the family ever put on a ledger.

drops.label: Last Fathom Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: The Court's Fang
drops.sublabel: Raid item. A tooth pried from one of the don’s court. On a CRITICAL hit, 20% chance to tear a loaded cannonball clean off the enemy’s rack, delaying its next shot.

drops.label: The Don’s Signet
drops.sublabel: Raid item. The ring every captain in the Finndicate answered to, and every gun in his court. On a CRITICAL hit, the command turns against them: 50% chance to tear a loaded cannonball off the enemy’s rack, delaying its next shot.

detail.dropsNote: One crate per clear, rolled once and scaled by your Fortune. The Don's Signet is the signature chase. The ring the whole Finndicate answered to. Two stronger Tide events between fights.

nodes.label: Challenge: The Throne
nodes.flavor: The court reconvenes, and this time the don skips the pleasantries.

detail.description: The Throne again, meaner in every seat. Thicker barriers, heavier ultimates, the same aim-bar tricks with less patience between them. And the don rises twice as angry. The chase rewards roll richer.

drops.label: Last Fathom Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: The Court's Fang
drops.sublabel: Raid item. A tooth pried from one of the don’s court. On a CRITICAL hit, 20% chance to tear a loaded cannonball clean off the enemy’s rack, delaying its next shot.

drops.label: The Don’s Signet
drops.sublabel: Raid item. The ring every captain in the Finndicate answered to, and every gun in his court. On a CRITICAL hit, the command turns against them: 50% chance to tear a loaded cannonball off the enemy’s rack, delaying its next shot.

detail.dropsNote: Every kill pays more and the clear bonus is steeper than the normal run.

nodes.label: Between Watches
nodes.flavor: The don's court on the seabed and a whole crew on the deck that put it there. But before the grog is even cold, something out past the wreck rises to watch, and is gone before you can be sure it was there.
nodes.bridge: One tide ends. The Finndicate is drowned, the crew is whole, and whatever watched from the deep can wait for morning.

scene.text: The megalodon goes down the way an empire does. A long time proud, and then no time at all.
He is still going down when he finds the breath for one more.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Let him talk. Let the sea hear him say it.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: You think you have taken something off me. I only ever held the knife, captain.

scene.speaker: Don Finleone
scene.text: You have not met the Hand that sharpens it.
And then the court scatters, the colors strike, and generations of drowned debts sink to the bottom with the don who collected them.
Then, out past the wreck, where the don's water spills over into the true deep, the black surface stirs. Something is watching the ruin you made, and it was never once in his court.
It rises just enough to throw a shape against the dark: a figure standing easy with one arm out over the water, a stance you would swear you had seen before on sunnier water, over a far shorter line.
The don was the biggest name in the sea. He was not your last fight.
And something in the shape of the whole chase shifts, the way a word you have said a thousand times goes strange in your mouth. You could not say what moved. Only that it did.
Then the deep folds over it, and it is gone before you can be sure it was ever there at all.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Captain. Tell me you saw that too. ...No. Not tonight. Tonight the don's on the bottom, and that was us. The rest can keep till morning.
The court settles to the seabed, and for the first time in four chapters, there is nothing ahead to point at. So the crew takes the longest watch of all. Together.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: I've sailed this sea longer than any of you have drawn breath, and I never once believed I'd see the Finndicate on the bottom. Well done, small fry.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Don't let him fool you. He's crying. Whales do that.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: The biggest bounty in the sea, collected, and I got to be there for it. I could get used to this crew.

scene.speaker: Dole
scene.text: Four chapters, one drowned empire, and a debt the whole sea owed finally paid in full. The finest sum I ever balanced.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: The drowned can rest now. All the captains the don fed to this water. That's worth more than any coin in his vault.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: All of us, one impossible mark, and a captain with no sense of self-preservation. I've never had better odds in my life.
Tonight the crew is whole, the grog is cold, and the whole sea knows your name. Whatever waited out past the wreck can wait for morning.

detail.description: Don Finleone is drowned and the Finndicate broken with him, the biggest name in the sea answered for. And then, out past the wreck at the lip of the true deep, a figure that was never in the don's court rises just long enough to watch, then sinks: he was not your last fight. But that is tomorrow's tide. Tonight all six of you take the longest watch together, and for once the crew is whole.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment XIV
drops.sublabel: "The don is drowned, and that was us. Something out past the wreck rose to watch. Tomorrow. Tonight the crew is whole."

detail.dropsNote: The don falls, something out past the wreck rises to watch, and the crew takes the longest watch together.
detail.summary: Don Finleone is drowned and the Finndicate broken, the biggest name in the sea answered for. A figure that was never in his court rises past the wreck to watch, then sinks: he was not your last fight. But that is tomorrow. Tonight the whole crew takes the longest watch together, and the whole sea knows your name.

nodes.label: The Don's Shipwright
nodes.flavor: The don kept a shipwright the way other captains keep a surgeon. He works for you now. One last refit, bolted to your deck for good.
nodes.bridge: The plans are cut and the iron is on the deck. One more mount, if you want to pay for it.

detail.description:
The finest shipwright on the drowned market owes you his freedom, and he pays it in iron. He can cut your deck for one more RAID-ITEM MOUNT: an extra piece of gear working every fight, on every raid from here on.

It costs a fortune. Take his plans to your shipwrights in Manage Ship when you are ready to pay for it.
detail.dropsNote: A permanent extra raid-item mount, on every raid. Bought once in Manage Ship, and it never comes off.
detail.summary: The don's shipwright owes you his freedom and pays it in iron: an extra RAID-ITEM MOUNT cut into your deck for a fortune, one more piece of gear working every fight. Buy it in Manage Ship.

nodes.label: The Hand That Sharpens It
nodes.flavor: Six giants came up out of the Ancient Deep on your line, and every one of them went somewhere. You never once asked where. The don said you had not met the Hand yet. He was right, and he was not warning you.
nodes.bridge: The sea is very quiet now, and every quiet thing you ever pulled up out of the dark was a favor you did not know you were doing.

scene.text: The sixth giant is on your wall, and the sea has been quiet ever since. No pirates. No fog. A whole ocean waiting on something.
Then a heading comes. Not a vault, not a fortress. Just open water in good morning light.
There is a small boat on it, with someone sitting in the stern and a line in the water. Whoever it is does not turn around when you come alongside.

scene.speaker: The Angler
scene.text: Took you long enough. I'd about run out of water to wait on.
You know that voice. You cannot place it out here, but you know it.
He turns around.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Surprised? Heh.
Finn.
The loudmouth off your own dock. The one who laughs at your boat every morning and tells you where the real fish are.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Finn?! *You* were behind all of this?

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: But you are... you're just a fisher. You sit on a dock all day.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: How is this possible? You orchestrated all of it? You were the one pulling the strings on someone as powerful as the don?

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: The don was a very big fish in a very small pond, and he did exactly what I paid him to do.
Mira has not said a word. She is staring at nothing, the way she does when a number will not sit right.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: The ledger.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: That one letter, signed under every crooked page of it. I told you it was a dead partner. I *swore* to you.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: F.
And you watch it land on her.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: ...Oh no. No, no, no. The F. The *Finn*dicate. It has had his name written on it the entire time.
Nobody says anything at all for a moment.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: The lot of you. Chasing it up the ladder that whole way, and not one of you ever once said it out loud. Most never do. Not until it is far too late to help them.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: You want to know why. Everyone does, right at the end.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: The ancients. That is all any of it was ever for.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Every shipment. Every crooked cargo. Every captain I bought and every hold I filled. All of it was gear and coin and charts, spent finding the old ones and trying to reach them.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: The whole Finndicate. Generations of it. That was your *tackle box*.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: A whole lifetime of my own poured into it, and the deep still would not let me near them.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: It will not open for me. It never has. So I needed someone it *would* open for.
He looks at you the way he looks at a good catch.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: You tore through my captains like they were nothing. Every one I put in your way. That alone would have been worth watching.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: But then you kept fishing. You put in the hours, you got good, and you got good enough to land what sleeps down there. Six for six.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I did not think anything in this ocean could do both. You impressed me, captain. Truly.
It is the first honest thing he has said, and somehow it is the worst one.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: So I let you run. Every door you kicked down, I left unlocked. You cleared out my own house and called it a campaign, and you got sharper every time you did it.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Captain. Whatever he wants, he is not getting it.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: You're carrying them right now. Did you never wonder why they never rotted?
He lifts one hand, and the six of them come up out of your hold on their own.
They hang in a ring around him, turning slow, the way they must have turned down in the dark.
Then, one at a time, in the order you caught them, the power goes out of them and into him.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: He's ABSORBING them. Those slept down there before there were charts to leave them off, and he is taking every last thing they had.
The sea flattens. Every wave for a league around lies down at once, like the water is holding still to let it happen.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: The hold. Captain, the hold is EMPTY.
What comes down on the water afterward is only the shape. Gray and light and wrong, like driftwood.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Finally.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: A lifetime of waiting. *Finally.* The power I have been longing for.
Something goes wrong with the way he is standing there.
The color drains out of him first. Then the shape starts to go, and what is left of it will not hold still.
He gets bigger. Not all at once. The way a swell gets bigger, when you already know it is going to break over you.
Light opens along him in cracks, like something inside is too big for the shell it borrowed.
The morning goes white, and then it goes dark from him outward.
A lifetime of dockside angler was a costume. This is what was wearing it.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: No... no, it can't be...

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: All this time we thought we had wiped the Finndicate off the sea. Every captain, every cache, every ledger. It was him. It was only ever him.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: I have been drowned, captain. I know what the deep feels like. It is standing in front of us.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: I have swum this sea longer than any of you have drawn breath, and I have never felt anything like that. There is nothing left in this ocean that can close this.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Ah. There it is.
The water pulls back from the boat. Even the deep is giving him room.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Every cold thing at the bottom of this ocean answers to me now. I can feel the whole of it, all the way down, like it is sitting in my hands.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Six keys, and the door is open, and I am already through it. You did that. Remember that you did that.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: And I want it said plainly, in front of your whole crew, because you have earned the hearing of it.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: You hunted them. You hauled them up out of the dark one at a time. You carried them in your own hold and kept them safe for me the entire way.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Captain. Do not let him talk.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: The finest crew that ever put out of that harbor, and every hour of it went into earning me this. Thank you. Truly. You have my gratitude, for whatever you think that is worth out here.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: He is thanking us.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: It was always going to be mine. You just did the rowing.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: You'll come after me. You have never once done the sensible thing, and I built all of this on it.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: One last ride, then. You and me and the deep. You'll be on time. You always are.
The dark holds where the morning was. Six gray shapes turn slow circles on the water.
You came out here for the last name on the board. You have had it since the day you started.

detail.description:
The last stop is not on any chart the Finndicate kept. It opens for a captain who has been down where the old things sleep, and it opens for nobody else.

That was always the point.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Fragment XV
drops.sublabel: "Everyone hears the name eventually. Never once before it is too late to matter."

detail.dropsNote: The name at the top of the Sunken Hand, and what your six giants were really for.
detail.summary: What the six giants were really for. Opens only once every Ancient Deep trophy is on your wall.

nodes.label: The Sunken Hand
nodes.flavor: No ledger, no lieutenant, no don between you. Just the water, a long quiet line, and the angler on the other end of it who has been reeling the whole time.

detail.description: One last ride, captain. Everything the Sunken Hand ever took, and everything it opened for you, comes down to this water.

drops.label: The Primeval Eye
drops.sublabel: Fishing special. Cut out of him still open, and still looking. It gains a TIER for every stretch of Navigation XP you earn while it is seated, and each tier keeps everything the tiers below it unlocked. Six in all.

drops.label: The Primeval Maw
drops.sublabel: Raid item. The oldest teeth in the sea, cut back out of what wore them and bolted to your hull. It gains a TIER for every stretch of Fishing XP you earn while it is mounted, and each tier keeps everything the tiers below it unlocked. Six in all.

drops.label: Sunken Hand Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Tundra Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

drops.label: Volcanic Hull
drops.sublabel: Ship skin. A cosmetic new look for your ship.

detail.dropsNote: Everything the six giants gave him, taken back off his hull.
detail.summary: The last fight. Read The Hand That Sharpens It first.

nodes.label: The Long Quiet
nodes.flavor: The water where he stood will not hold a wave. Your crew are still braced for a fight that is already over, and nobody has said anything yet.
nodes.bridge: Six giants went into him. They are coming back out, and the sea is taking them home.

scene.text: The last shot lands, and nothing happens for a moment.
Then his hull gives. Not split, not burned. It simply stops arguing with the sea.
It goes over slow, the way a big thing goes over, and the water closes on it without a sound.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: ...impossible.
He is still standing. He is standing on nothing at all, and he has not noticed.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: How could you defeat me...?
The light that was running under his skin turns and starts going the other way.
It leaves through the same cracks it opened. Six of them, one at a time, in the order you caught them.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I had all of it. Every cold thing at the bottom of this ocean. I had it in my *hands*.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: A lifetime. I gave a whole lifetime to the waiting...
He looks at you the way he did on the dock, every morning, for years.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: ...you were never supposed to be better than me at this.
And then there is nothing there to look back at.
What is left of him goes up rather than down, gray and weightless, and the wind takes it apart before it clears the mast.
And then the water is quiet, and there is a small boat sitting on it.
Someone is in the stern, the way someone was the first morning you came alongside. No color to him. No weight to him either.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Heh.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: Would you look at that. All of it gone, and this is what's left underneath.
It is just Finn. The loudmouth off your dock, sat in his own little boat with no line in the water.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: Captain... he looks like he used to.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I was, once. Same as you.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: I too was just an angler at first...
He is going. You can see the light through him now.

scene.speaker: Finn
scene.text: ...don't let it get to you too...
Nobody asks him what he means. There is nobody left in the boat to ask.
It rides there empty for a moment, level and unhurried, and then the sea takes that as well.
The sea comes back in. One long swell rolls through where he was, and the ocean is just an ocean again.
For a while your crew just stand there, still braced.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: ...Is that it? Is it done?

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: The ledger's shut. Every page of it traced back to one name, and that name is not in the water any more.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: He sat on that dock. He watched us leave every single morning. He waved.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: He waved at me too. I always thought he was being friendly.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: He was. That was the worst part of him.
Somebody laughs. It is not a good laugh, but it is a real one, and it lets the rest of them breathe.

scene.speaker: Mira
scene.text: Captain. The six are gone from the hold. Properly gone, this time.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Not gone. Home.
Doby is looking down, past the boat, at water that has no bottom worth speaking of.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: The deep gave them up for him because he asked with your hands. It has them back now.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: Something down there let go of them twice, captain. Once for him, and once just now.

scene.speaker: Doby
scene.text: I would not call that an empty ocean.
Nobody picks it up. The light is good and the water is flat and everyone is very tired.

scene.speaker: Kat
scene.text: Then we go home. That's the whole plan. We go home.

scene.speaker: Mako
scene.text: I could sleep for a week.

scene.speaker: Laz
scene.text: You have slept for a week. Twice.
The crew turn the boat around without being told, the way they have a hundred times.
Behind you the water lies down flat and stays that way, all the way to the horizon.
You came out here for the last name on the board. There is nothing written on it now.
It is a long quiet ride back, and every hour of it is yours.

detail.description:
The Sunken Hand is closed. The name at the top of it is not in this ocean any more, and the six he took have gone back down where you found them.

What he left behind is still on the water, and it will still fit a captain who knows what to do with it.

drops.label: Captain's Logbook, Final Entry
drops.sublabel: "Fair weather the whole way home. Crew asleep on the deck, all of them, in the sun. Nothing on the horizon. Writing it down so I remember that it happened."

detail.dropsNote: The end of the Sunken Hand, and the last page of the log.
detail.summary: The end of it. Then take what he left behind.

nodes.label: The Spoils of the Hand
nodes.flavor: Two things came up off his wreck, and only one of them will fit aboard today. The other keeps.
nodes.bridge: One is a reel. One is a mount. Both were his, and neither was meant for you.

detail.description:
He went down with two things worth taking, and they answer to the two halves of your life out here.

THE DEEP REEL opens a SECOND special slot on your fishing rig, and only The Primeval Eye will seat in it.

THE SIXTH MOUNT frames one more raid item onto your hull, and only The Primeval Maw will mount there.

Neither tool is in your hold yet. This opens the berth. The wreck still has to give the piece up.

Take one now. The other keeps, and it keeps expensive.
detail.summary: Choose one of his two spoils. The other costs 2,500,000 doubloons.
detail.dropsNote: Each slot fits exactly one item, and that item only ever drops from him.

nodes.label: Challenge: One Last Ride
nodes.flavor: He is still down there, and the water still remembers the shape of him. Go again, with none of the mercy.

detail.description: Six phases, six stolen giants, and a chain you cannot afford to drop. Everything he does hits harder and his own rhythm is tighter, so the Perfect Streak stops being a reward and starts being the requirement.

chapters.title: The Loose Thread
chapters.subtitle: A coast full of pirates, and a thread that runs to somewhere bigger.

chapters.title: A Bigger Fish

chapters.title: One Last Ride
chapters.subtitle: The don was never the top of it. Something has been waiting on you since the first cast.
